Mechanistic analyses indicated that Nb74 neutralizes virus by blocking viral attachment to the host. Furthermore, combined hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) with escape mutant analysis mapped its epitope to a conserved lateral patch on the HA1 subunit, consistent with a conformational epitope. Overall, these results demonstrate the therapeutic promise of intratracheally delivered Nb74 and provide insights for H7 AIVs vaccine design. IMPORTANCE H7 avian influenza viruses (AIVs), including both low- and highly pathogenic strains, pose a persistent threat to poultry production and public health, while continuous antigenic evolution of the HA1 subunit undermines vaccine effectiveness. Broadly neutralizing agents against H7 AIVs are urgently needed for pandemic preparedness, yet nanobody-based therapeutics remain largely unexplored. In this study, we identified Nb74, a nanobody that inhibits hemagglutination and neutralizes multiple H7 strains. Importantly, intratracheal delivery of Nb74 conferred protective efficacy, supporting respiratory administration of nanobody therapeutics. Mechanistic analyses show that Nb74 blocks viral attachment by recognizing a conserved conformational epitope within a lateral patch of the HA1 subunit. These findings reveal a conserved and functionally vulnerable region on H7 hemagglutinin (HA) and support the development of nanobody-based antivirals and improved vaccine strategies against emerging H7 AIV threats.

papers.title: Geographic Concentration of Genomic Surveillance for Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5), South Asia, 2015-2025
papers.abstract: Early detection of mammalian adaptation in highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5) depends on genomic surveillance, yet its distribution across high-burden regions is poorly characterized. We quantified open-access (GenBank/INSDC) H5 genomic coverage relative to reported outbreak burden across nine South Asian countries during 2015-2025, linking isolates to FAO EMPRES-i/WOAH events. Of 919 H5 isolates, 814 (89%) came from one country (Bangladesh); the other eight contributed 105. India, with the largest burden (322 events), yielded only 42 isolates (13 per 100); Nepal, 2 of 78; Afghanistan, none of 5. Concentration was extreme (Gini 0.83) and unchanged by adding restricted GISAID records (1,297 combined isolates; Bangladesh 89%) or by normalizing to poultry or human population. Because reported outbreaks track reporting effort, these coverage ratios are directional, not rates. This single-country dependency, deepest where burden is highest, is a regional early-warning vulnerability.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the geographic concentration of genomic surveillance for highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5) in South Asia from 2015 to 2025. It highlights that while genomic surveillance is critical for early detection of mammalian adaptation, its distribution is uneven, with Bangladesh contributing the majority of isolates. The findings reveal that countries with high outbreak burdens, such as India, have significantly lower genomic coverage compared to others. The extreme concentration of data in Bangladesh, even when considering additional isolates or normalizing to population size, indicates a potential vulnerability in early warning systems. The study underscores the need for more equitable genomic surveillance efforts across the region to improve preparedness and response to avian influenza outbreaks.

papers.title: Negotiating security and resilience: Planning conundrums for avian influenza control in Great Britain's poultry systems
papers.abstract: Abstract The outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza in Great Britain between 2021 and 2026 represent the most severe period of virus activity recorded in the country, prompting renewed scrutiny of how biosecurity is conceptualised and practised within poultry systems. This paper examines how the structure of poultry sectors, producing meat, eggs, and game birds, shape disease risk and the possibilities for a resilient poultry ecology. Using a production and distribution network approach, we combine a desk-based review of industry, policy, grey, and published literature with qualitative data from 19 in-depth interviews, supplemented by field visits and engagement in stakeholder events. Our analysis shows that highly integrated and geographically concentrated poultry meat and layer systems interact with wild and semi-wild birds in ways which generate distinct challenges. Concentration of production and processing infrastructure, aging housing stock, consumer demand for free-range, and large-scale releases of game birds impact decisions around poultry governance and questions of risk around avian influenza incursion. We identify two cross-cutting ‘entanglements’ that condition avian influenza virus vulnerability: (1) poultry planning, where fragmented and often contested land-use decisions interact with environmental and biodiversity policies to shape exposure to wild and semi-wild ecologies; and (2) the insuring of poultry, where a market failure in private avian influenza insurance and uneven and contested state compensation regimes differentially distribute risk across producers and sectors. We argue that farm-level biosecurity, while necessary, is insufficient to secure Britain’s poultry production under near-endemic avian influenza virus pressure. A more bio-resilient poultry future will require macro-level, multi-sectoral coordination that integrates spatial planning, infrastructure renewal, and equitable risk-sharing mechanisms for disease preparedness.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreaks in Great Britain (2021-2026), examining how poultry sector structures (meat, eggs, game birds) shape disease risk and ecological resilience. The central question is how biosecurity conceptualization and practice can be improved under near-endemic virus pressure.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The paper employs a production and distribution network approach, combining a desk-based review of industry, policy, grey, and published literature with qualitative data from 19 in-depth interviews, supplemented by field visits and stakeholder engagement.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Highly integrated and geographically concentrated poultry systems interact with wild/semi-wild birds, creating distinct challenges. Two cross-cutting 'entanglements' shape vulnerability: (1) poultry planning, where fragmented land-use decisions interact with environmental policies, and (2) insurance mechanisms, where market failures and uneven state compensation distribute risk inequitably. Farm-level biosecurity alone is insufficient.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The analysis identifies tensions between consumer demand for free-range products, aging housing stock, and large-scale game bird releases, which complicate governance decisions. No explicit methodological limitations are reported, but the reliance on qualitative data may limit generalizability.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: A bio-resilient poultry future requires macro-level, multi-sectoral coordination integrating spatial planning, infrastructure renewal, and equitable risk-sharing mechanisms for disease preparedness.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines avian influenza outbreaks in Great Britain (2021-2026), analyzing how poultry sector structures influence disease risk and resilience. Using mixed methods (literature review, 19 interviews, field visits), the research identifies two key 'entanglements': (1) fragmented land-use planning interacting with environmental policies, and (2) inequitable insurance mechanisms distributing risk unevenly. The authors conclude that farm-level biosecurity is insufficient under near-endemic virus pressure, advocating for macro-level coordination involving spatial planning, infrastructure renewal, and equitable risk-sharing to achieve bio-resilience.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究重点关注英国的 高致病性禽流感 暴发(2021-2026 年),研究家禽业结构(肉、蛋、猎禽)如何影响疾病风险和生态恢复力。核心问题是如何在近乎流行的病毒压力下改进生物安全概念和实践。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本文采用生产和分销网络方法,将对行业、政策、灰色和已发表文献的案头审查与 19 次深度访谈的定性数据相结合,并辅以实地访问和利益相关者参与。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 高度集成和地理集中的家禽系统与野生/半 野生鸟类 相互作用,带来了独特的挑战。两个交叉的“纠缠”形成了脆弱性:(1) 家禽规划,其中分散的土地使用决策与环境政策相互作用;(2) 保险机制,其中市场失灵和不均匀的国家补偿不公平地分配风险。仅农场一级的生物安全是不够的。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该分析确定了消费者对散养产品的需求、老化的住房存量和大规模野鸟放归之间的紧张关系,这使治理决策变得复杂。没有报告明确的方法学限制,但对定性数据的依赖可能会限制普遍性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 具有生物抵抗力的家禽未来需要宏观层面的多部门协调,整合空间规划、基础设施更新和疾病预防的公平风险分担机制。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 2021 年至 2026 年英国 高致病性禽流感 的 暴发 代表了该国有记录的病毒活动最严重的时期,促使人们重新审视如何在家禽系统中概念化和实施生物安全。本文研究了生产肉类、蛋类和猎禽的家禽部门的结构如何影响疾病风险以及弹性家禽生态的可能性。我们采用生产和分销网络方法,将对行业、政策、灰色和已发表文献的案头审查与来自 19 次深度访谈的定性数据结合起来,并辅以实地考察和参与利益相关者活动。我们的分析表明,高度集成和地理集中的家禽肉和蛋鸡系统与野生和半 野生鸟类 相互作用,产生了独特的挑战。生产和加工基础设施的集中、住房存量老化、消费者对散养的需求以及野禽的大规模释放影响着家禽治理的决策以及 禽流感 入侵的风险问题。我们确定了影响 禽流感 病毒脆弱性的两个交叉“纠缠”:(1)家禽规划,其中分散且经常有争议的土地利用决策与环境和生物多样性政策相互作用,以塑造野生和半野生生态的暴露程度;(2) 家禽保险,其中私人 禽流感 保险的市场失灵以及不平衡且有争议的国家赔偿制度在生产者和部门之间分配了不同的风险。我们认为,农场层面的生物安全虽然必要,但不足以在近乎流行的 禽流感 病毒压力下确保英国的家禽生产。更具生物弹性的家禽未来将需要宏观层面的多部门协调,将空间规划、基础设施更新和疾病防备的公平风险分担机制结合起来。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究重点关注英国的 高致病性禽流感 暴发(2021-2026 年),研究家禽业结构(肉、蛋、猎禽)如何影响疾病风险和生态恢复力。核心问题是如何在近乎流行的病毒压力下改进生物安全概念和实践。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本文采用生产和分销网络方法,将对行业、政策、灰色和已发表文献的案头审查与 19 次深度访谈的定性数据相结合,并辅以实地访问和利益相关者参与。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 高度集成和地理集中的家禽系统与野生/半 野生鸟类 相互作用,带来了独特的挑战。两个交叉的“纠缠”形成了脆弱性:(1) 家禽规划,其中分散的土地使用决策与环境政策相互作用;(2) 保险机制,其中市场失灵和不均匀的国家补偿不公平地分配风险。仅农场一级的生物安全是不够的。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该分析确定了消费者对散养产品的需求、老化的住房存量和大规模野鸟放归之间的紧张关系,这使治理决策变得复杂。没有报告明确的方法学限制,但对定性数据的依赖可能会限制普遍性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 具有生物抵抗力的家禽未来需要宏观层面的多部门协调,整合空间规划、基础设施更新和疾病预防的公平风险分担机制。

papers.title: Peru’s only penguin species at risk from upcoming El Niño and bird flu, experts warn
papers.abstract: SAN JUAN DE MARCONA, Peru — First, there was the H5N1 avian influenza of 2022, then El Niño arrived in 2023, disrupting coastal waters and fish availability. For Peru’s Humboldt penguins, the only species of penguins that breeds in the country, the burden was too heavy: Its population dropped by two-thirds between 2022 and 2025.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the impact of H5N1 avian influenza and El Niño on Peru's Humboldt penguin population, highlighting a significant decline as a pressing conservation concern.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research focuses on Peru's Humboldt penguins, the only penguin species breeding in the country, with population data tracked between 2022 and 2025.
analysis.methods: The study analyzes population trends and environmental disruptions, specifically examining the effects of H5N1 avian influenza and El Niño on the penguins' habitat and food availability.
analysis.main_results: Peru's Humboldt penguin population decreased by two-thirds between 2022 and 2025, attributed to the combined impacts of H5N1 avian influenza and El Niño.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the decline as a direct consequence of dual stressors, emphasizing the unprecedented vulnerability of this species to concurrent environmental and disease-related threats.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the need for enhanced surveillance of avian influenza and climate-related impacts on endangered species, informing conservation strategies and zoonotic disease monitoring.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to observational population data without detailed mechanistic studies, resulting in moderate confidence due to the lack of controlled analysis.

analysis.summary_en: Peru's Humboldt penguin population has declined by two-thirds between 2022 and 2025, primarily due to the combined effects of H5N1 avian influenza and El Niño. The avian influenza outbreak in 2022 and subsequent El Niño event disrupted coastal waters and fish availability, creating an unsustainable burden on the only penguin species breeding in Peru. Experts warn that these dual threats highlight the species' extreme vulnerability, necessitating urgent conservation measures and enhanced surveillance for both avian influenza and climate-related impacts on marine ecosystems.

Facebook Linkedin Threads Whatsapp Reddit Email Page link Cite article The Humboldt penguin is the only penguin species to breed in Peru, inhabiting the country’s coastal deserts. But since 2022, the species’ has been under pressure from the spread of avian influenza, followed by El Niño.Between 2022 and 2025, the population of Humboldt penguins has dropped by two-thirds across 34 islands and peninsulas on the Peruvian coast.Experts monitoring the species say penguins are abandoning their nests as they already feel the impacts of the upcoming El Niño episode, which changes temperatures in coastal waters and diminishes the amount of prey fish available.Scientists are asking both the national government and the IUCN to revise the species’ status to reflect the increasing threats and boost conservation efforts.See All Key Ideas SAN JUAN DE MARCONA, Peru — First, there was the H5N1 avian influenza of 2022, then El Niño arrived in 2023, disrupting coastal waters and fish availability. For Peru’s Humboldt penguins, the only species of penguins that breeds in the country, the burden was too heavy: Its population dropped by two-thirds between 2022 and 2025. Still recovering, the species is now facing a super El Niño that could further undermine its future. In early June, the Secretary-General of the United Nations, António Guterres, warned: “The science is clear: El Niño is arriving on our doorstep in the coming months with 90% certainty. The world must treat it as the urgent climate warning it is. El Niño conditions will pour fuel on the fire of a warming world. Impacts will hit even harder, travel even farther, and cross borders with devastating speed.” Scientists studying the Humboldt penguins (Spheniscus humboldti) in Peru say that they are already feeling the impact of the 2026 El Niño as warmer coastal waters drive the cold current carrying the main prey fish, Peruvian anchovy (Engraulis ringens) or anchoveta, deeper and further offshore. That means the penguins and other seabirds are forced to undertake longer fishing trips to get enough food to breed or feed chicks. Scientists studying El Niño say the gaps between the events are getting smaller and the effects are more unpredictable. “Climate change is driving more frequent and more severe El Niño events,” Andres Lescano, director of Clima, the Latin American Center of Excellence in Climate Change and Health, told Mongabay. The Humboldt penguin nests and rests in the coastal deserts of southern Peru and northern Chile’s arid Pacific coastline and offshore islands, which are directly affected by El Niño events. In Punta San Juan de Marcona National Reserve, one of the penguins’ major nesting colonies in southern Peru, the number of penguin nests has halved between April and May 2026, from 190 on April 10 to 94 on May 30, according to scientists’ recordings. “They abandoned their nests,” Peruvian biologist Susana Cardénas, the director of the Punta San Juan program, told Mongabay at the 54-hectare (133 acres) marine reserve, where she leads a team that monitors the Humboldt penguin population. El Niño undermines food availability for the Humboldt penguin, leading to breeding failure and nest abandonment. Image courtesy of Punta San Juan program. Image by Ann Knutson. “There was a reduction in food availability and when the parent that stays with the egg gets too hungry, it leaves,” she said. “The [Humboldt] penguin is the sentinel species, and its breeding failure is a sign that it’s going to get worse. It’s going to be a really bad year for all the seabirds.” The Humboldt penguin breeds from April to August and from September until December, before other seabirds, so it is the first to be impacted by the shortage of food caused by the warmer sea surface temperatures, which have risen by up to 2° Celsius (3.6° Fahrenheit) in the eastern equatorial Pacific, according to Peru’s official National Study of the El Niño Phenomenon. Punta San Juan de Marcona serves as a marine biodiversity hotspot with large breeding populations of seabirds, including the Humboldt penguin, the Peruvian pelican (Pelecanus thagus), the Guanay cormorant (Leucocarbo bougainvillii), the Peruvian booby (Sula variegata), and hundreds-strong breeding colonies of Peruvian fur seal (Arctocephalus australis ssp) and South American sea lions (Otaria byronia), as well as a small population of marine otters (Lontra felina). The Humboldt current, which flows up from Antarctica, allows the upwelling of nutrients, which supports a huge biomass of anchoveta as well as a variety of seabirds, sea lions and fur seals. Peru’s coast is one of the third or fourth richest fisheries in the world. However, as sea surface temperatures began to rise, Peru’s Production and Fisheries Ministry announced on June 11 that it was closing the anchoveta fishing season in the country’s north-central coast as a “conservation measure” based on scientific information from the Peruvian Sea Institute (IMARPE). The burden of disease After the H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) hit South America in late 2022, the virus caused a massive drop in seabird and marine mammal numbers in 2022 and 2023, on its Pacific and Atlantic coasts. In Peru alone, the virus killed about 558,000 seabirds across 14 species (including cormorants, boobies, pelicans, seagulls, terns and penguins) and 11,000 sea lions between December 2022 and December 2023, according to a 2025 study published by the Society for Conservation Biology. Peru’s seabird population was particularly hard hit, accounting for the vast majority of bird deaths, with an estimated 667,000 total on South America’s Pacific and Atlantic coasts. But bird species continued to be battered by the ensuing El Niño. As sea temperatures peaked at nearly 4 °C (7.2° F) higher than normal in the last year, penguins and other seabirds were forced to undertake longer fishing trips, often exposing the chicks or fledglings to predators, starvation, nest abandonment by the parent birds, or, in some cases, the shortage of food can mean that the penguins do not breed at all. In Punta San Juan, not a single penguin nest was recorded in 2023. “This is unprecedented since records began,” explained Cárdenas, who runs the Punta San Juan program through the Centre for Environmental Sustainability at Lima’s Cayetano Heredia University. “The penguins were getting ready for their breeding season; the marine conditions changed and they did not come back to breed.” The Humboldt penguin is the only penguin species breeding in Peru. Image courtesy of the Punta San Juan program. Image by Michael Tweddle. A census of the penguins in 34 islands and peninsulas along the Peruvian coast showed that their numbers dropped from 15,663 in 2022 to approximately 5,400 in 2025, according to a census carried out by Cayetano Heredia University and the NGO Peruvian Association for the Conservation of Nature (APECO) and other organizations, along with Peru’s Forestry and Wildlife Service, SERFOR. Since 2023, constant monitoring of the population by scientists at the Punta San Juan reserve has detected a slow recovery in numbers, until the early effects of the 2026 El Niño caused a new wave of nest abandonment. In July, local Peruvian media was reporting the deaths of marine birds, including penguins, as well as marine mammals such as South American sea lions along the coast due to a lack of food. As the Humboldt Penguin faces an onslaught of threats, Cárdenas and other scientists in Peru are asking the government to change its conservation status from endangered to critically endangered. The move had been approved by a supreme decree in 2021, but it still needs presidential approval to be signed into law. Scientists from Peru and Chile are also pushing the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species to update the classification of the penguin from vulnerable to endangered amid the decline in its numbers. In January 2025, SERFOR announced a National Conservation Plan for the Humboldt penguin and the sea otter, but, despite a series of workshops with conservationists and environmental nonprofits, the plan has yet to be published. papers.title: Genetic determinants of cell- and egg-preferred replication in H3N2 canine influenza virus.
papers.abstract: The H3N2 canine influenza virus (CIV), which originated from avian influenza viruses and has circulated in dogs for over two decades, remains poorly understood in terms of its host adaptation mechanisms and cellular tropism. In this study, we isolated two phenotypically distinct H3N2 CIV strains (CX3 and CX12) from a canine respiratory disease outbreak. Although both were isolated using MDCK cells, CX3 showed higher replication efficiency and plaque-forming ability in MDCK cells, whereas CX12 replicated more efficiently in chicken embryos. Using reverse genetics, we identified the PB1 gene as a critical enhancer of viral polymerase activity and the HA gene as a key contributor to viral stability, both of which collectively mediate cell-preferred replication. These findings provide mechanistic insights into H3N2 CIV host adaptation and offer a foundation for future vaccine development.

papers.title: A lethal human H5N5 influenza virus isolate exhibits low pandemic risk traits
papers.abstract: In fall of 2025, a fatal infection of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus H5N5 occurred. To define the risk of this emerging virus to humans, we performed a comprehensive analysis based on our established triage. Serological analysis revealed that humans across all birth years had no detectable neutralizing antibodies to this H5N5 isolate. Further characterization revealed a lack of phenotypic signatures associated with epidemiologically successful influenza viruses in humans, including reduced replication in human airway cells and an avian-like pH of inactivation. Additionally, assessment of H5N5 in ferrets revealed a lack of direct contact transmission and moderate disease severity. H5N5 infection in ferrets with prior immunity against the 2009 H1N1 pandemic strain resulted in fewer clinical signs and reduced viral shedding. Together our data suggest that the current H5N5 HPAI lineage poses a low pandemic risk.

papers.source_body_en: In fall of 2025, a fatal infection of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) virus H5N5 occurred. To define the risk of this emerging virus to humans, we performed a comprehensive analysis based on our established triage. Serological analysis revealed that humans across all birth years had no detectable neutralizing antibodies to this H5N5 isolate. Further characterization revealed a lack of phenotypic signatures associated with epidemiologically successful influenza viruses in humans, including reduced replication in human airway cells and an avian-like pH of inactivation. Additionally, assessment of H5N5 in ferrets revealed a lack of direct contact transmission and moderate disease severity. H5N5 infection in ferrets with prior immunity against the 2009 H1N1 pandemic strain resulted in fewer clinical signs and reduced viral shedding. Together our data suggest that the current H5N5 HPAI lineage poses a low pandemic risk.

papers.title: The One Health Blind Spot at the Human‒Animal Interface in US Influenza Surveillance.
papers.abstract: Novel influenza A viruses have cost thousands of lives and billions of dollars of economic losses in the 21st century, and 2 of the past 4 pandemic influenza A viruses likely originated in animal populations on the North American continent. Despite this, the human and veterinary influenza surveillance systems in the United States are poorly connected and have fallen short of congressional mandates for data sharing and interoperability. This places the United States in a reactive posture that is focused on containment of outbreaks that have already occurred rather than proactive surveillance and prevention. The significant investments in surveillance infrastructure and genomic technologies spurred by the COVID-19 pandemic, along with the new National One Health Framework, present a unique opportunity to modernize influenza surveillance with a greater emphasis on the interconnectedness of human and animal health. However, funding for enhanced surveillance is set to decrease significantly as pandemic-era funding sunsets. Continuing investments into novel surveillance technologies have been critical in addressing the recent H5N1 influenza outbreaks and will be critical to prevent future economic losses and losses of both human and animal life. ( Am J Public Health . 2026;116(8):1220-1228. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308445).

However, funding for enhanced surveillance is set to decrease, threatening progress. papers.title: Evolution is Not Always Bifurcating: ATLAZ and the Geometric Resolution of Reticulate Virology
papers.abstract: Abstract The reliance on strictly bifurcating phylogenetic trees fundamentally distorts the evolutionary history of reticulate viral populations. Traditional maximum-likelihood algorithms mandate vertical descent, imposing artificial clades upon recombinant genomes and obscuring the origins of segmented pandemic shifts. Furthermore, linear selection metrics (e.g., dN/dS) fail mathematically when evaluating overlapping open reading frames. Here, ATLAZ (Alignment, Topology, and Lineage Analysis in Zig) is presented as a memory-deterministic geometric engine that explicitly bypasses the phylogenetic tree to track the major transition from tree-like to reticulate evolution. By computing Vietoris-Rips simplicial complexes and extracting H1 persistence directly from spatial distance matrices, ATLAZ definitively isolates horizontal recombination in Hepatitis B and Avian Influenza. Conversely, the absence of topological loops strictly proves the clonal descent of Ebola, Zika, and Marburg viruses. Utilizing a native Galois Field reduction across a zero-copy C-ABI boundary, ATLAZ processes massive cohorts (over 6,000 sequences) with memory strictly bounded by the sparse filtration cutoff, shattering the catastrophic computational bottlenecks of previous Topological Data Analysis frameworks. Furthermore, sequential column ablation calculates a novel Topological Selection Score (TSS), geometrically mapping absolute structural rigidity and identifying optimal targets for direct-acting antivirals in seconds. ATLAZ establishes a new absolute, math-driven standard for tracking major transitions in computational virology.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 对严格分叉的系统发育树的依赖从根本上扭曲了网状病毒种群的进化历史。传统的最大似然算法要求垂直下降,将人工进化枝强加于重组 基因组 上,并模糊了分段流行病转变的起源。此外,在评估重叠的开放阅读框时,线性选择指标(例如 dN/dS)在数学上会失败。在这里,ATLAZ(Zig 中的对齐、拓扑和谱系分析)被视为一种内存确定性几何引擎,它明确绕过系统发育树来跟踪从树状到网状 进化 的主要转变。通过计算 Vietoris-Rips 单纯复合体并直接从空间距离矩阵中提取 H1 持久性,ATLAZ 明确分离了乙型肝炎和 禽流感 中的水平重组。相反,拓扑环的缺失严格证明了埃博拉病毒、寨卡病毒和马尔堡病毒的克隆血统。利用跨零拷贝 C-ABI 边界的原生伽罗瓦域缩减,ATLAZ 可以处理大量 队列研究(超过 6,000 个序列),内存严格受稀疏过滤截断限制,打破了先前拓扑数据分析框架的灾难性计算瓶颈。此外,顺序列消融计算出一种新颖的拓扑选择分数(TSS),以几何方式映射绝对结构刚性并在几秒钟内确定直接作用的 抗病毒药物 的最佳目标。ATLAZ 建立了一个新的绝对的、数学驱动的标准,用于跟踪计算病毒学的重大转变。

papers.title: Elicitation of stem-directed antibodies in rhesus macaques by a conventional hemagglutinin immunogen
papers.abstract: Because they can bind many strains of influenza, antibodies targeting the hemagglutinin (HA) stem have been attractive targets for vaccine development. Many monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) directed at the HA stem have been isolated from humans, and these mAbs have mediated broad protection in animal models. We describe here HA stem-directed mAbs isolated from rhesus macaques immunized with an "ordinary" H1 HA trimer. All immunized rhesus macaques developed high serum titers with broad reactivity to diverse H1N1 and H5N1 viruses, and 7 isolated mAbs strongly blocked canonical stem antibody CR6261 binding to H1. MAb DH726.1 robustly protected mice from lethal challenge with H1N1 and H5N1 viruses, and cryo-EM showed the binding footprint overlapped that of some human mAbs. These findings suggest that vaccination with the standard, trimeric HA immunogens may be sufficient to elicit stem antibodies at titers adequate to protect against zoonotic H5N1 influenza.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore whether conventional hemagglutinin (HA) immunogens could elicit stem-directed antibodies in rhesus macaques, which are critical for broad protection against influenza viruses.

analysis.main_results: All immunized rhesus macaques developed high serum titers with broad reactivity to diverse H1N1 and H5N1 viruses, and 7 isolated mAbs strongly blocked canonical stem antibody CR6261 binding to H1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that vaccination with standard, trimeric HA immunogens may be sufficient to elicit stem antibodies at titers adequate to protect against zoonotic H5N1 influenza.

papers.source_body_en: Because they can bind many strains of influenza, antibodies targeting the hemagglutinin (HA) stem have been attractive targets for vaccine development. Many monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) directed at the HA stem have been isolated from humans, and these mAbs have mediated broad protection in animal models. We describe here HA stem-directed mAbs isolated from rhesus macaques immunized with an "ordinary" H1 HA trimer. All immunized rhesus macaques developed high serum titers with broad reactivity to diverse H1N1 and H5N1 viruses, and 7 isolated mAbs strongly blocked canonical stem antibody CR6261 binding to H1. MAb DH726.1 robustly protected mice from lethal challenge with H1N1 and H5N1 viruses, and cryo-EM showed the binding footprint overlapped that of some human mAbs. These findings suggest that vaccination with the standard, trimeric HA immunogens may be sufficient to elicit stem antibodies at titers adequate to protect against zoonotic H5N1 influenza.

papers.title: Integrated in silico and in vitro approaches reveal novel coumarin hybrids targeting influenza A virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat due to its high mutation rate and increasing resistance to existing antiviral drugs. The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is essential for viral replication and represents a promising target for new therapeutics. We screened our in-house chemical library of 103 compounds against two domains of the IAV RdRp complex using molecular docking. Based on computational findings, we selected eleven coumarin-phenolic acid hybrids and one thiazolidinone compounds for in vitro evaluation against H1N1 and H5N1. LMed 93 and LMed 99 exhibited potent antiviral activity, with EC 50 values of 5.66 and 1.21 μM against H1N1 respectively, and high selectivity indices. Mechanistic studies showed that LMed 99 acts throughout early to late stages of infection, while LMed 93 impacts early and intermediate stages. Both compounds significantly inhibited viral RNA synthesis, with LMed 99 achieving 82% inhibition at 1- and 3-hours post-infection (hpi) and 80% at 6 hpi, and LMed 93 achieving 82% (1 hpi), 78% (3 hpi), and 60% (6 hpi). LMed 99 reduced viral proteins and mRNA in a time-dependent manner, indicating interference with viral transcription. A mini-replicon assay showed that LMed 93, at 70 and 35 μM, reduces polymerase activity by 53.7% and 38.7%, while LMed 99 at 9 and 4.5 μM increased expression by 108.97% and 61.37%, respectively. Structure–activity relationship analysis highlighted that catechol groups and halogenation enhance antiviral potency. These findings suggest that LMed 93 and LMed 99 are promising coumarin-based scaffolds for developing new anti-Influenza A agents, also offering potential strategies for combating other RNA viruses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于 突变 的高发病率以及对现有 抗病毒药物 药物的耐药性不断增加,甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 仍然是一个重大的公共卫生威胁。该研究旨在鉴定针对 IAV RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 的新型化合物来应对这一挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用计算机和体外方法来筛选针对 IAV RdRp 复合物的化合物。它重点关注 禽流感 A 病毒,特别是 H5N1,并评估了所选化合物的 抗病毒药物 体外活性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员利用分子对接筛选了针对 IAV RdRp 复合物两个结构域的 103 种化合物。根据计算结果,他们选择了 11 种香豆素-酚酸杂化物和一种噻唑烷酮化合物,用于针对 H1N1 和 H5N1 的体外评估。
elements_zh.main_results: LMed 93 和 LMed 99 表现出有效的 抗病毒药物 活性,针对 H1N1 的 EC 50 值分别为 5.66 和 1.21 μM,并且具有高选择性指数。两种化合物均显着抑制病毒 RNA 合成,LMed 99 在感染后 1 小时和 3 小时 (hpi) 时实现了 82% 的抑制,在 6 hpi 时实现了 80% 的抑制,LMed 93 实现了 82% (1 hpi)、78% (3 hpi) 和 60% (6 hpi)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,LMed 93 和 LMed 99 是有前途的基于香豆素的支架,可用于开发新型抗甲型流感药物,为对抗其他 RNA 病毒提供潜在策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果为针对 IAV RdRp 的新 抗病毒药物 药物的开发提供了见解,这可以增强 禽流感 暴发 的 监测 和 治疗 选项。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外研究结果和计算筛选,可能无法完全反映体内疗效。证据是中等的,因为它不包括临床试验或长期影响。

papers.title_zh: 综合计算机和体外方法揭示了针对甲型流感病毒 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶的新型香豆素杂合体。
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT: Influenza A virus (IAV) remains a significant public health threat due to its high mutation rate and increasing resistance to existing antiviral drugs. The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is essential for viral replication and represents a promising target for new therapeutics. We screened our in-house chemical library of 103 compounds against two domains of the IAV RdRp complex using molecular docking. Based on computational findings, we selected eleven coumarin-phenolic acid hybrids and one thiazolidinone compounds for in vitro evaluation against H1N1 and H5N1. LMed 93 and LMed 99 exhibited potent antiviral activity, with EC 50 values of 5.66 and 1.21 μM against H1N1 respectively, and high selectivity indices. Mechanistic studies showed that LMed 99 acts throughout early to late stages of infection, while LMed 93 impacts early and intermediate stages. Both compounds significantly inhibited viral RNA synthesis, with LMed 99 achieving 82% inhibition at 1- and 3-hours post-infection (hpi) and 80% at 6 hpi, and LMed 93 achieving 82% (1 hpi), 78% (3 hpi), and 60% (6 hpi). LMed 99 reduced viral proteins and mRNA in a time-dependent manner, indicating interference with viral transcription. A mini-replicon assay showed that LMed 93, at 70 and 35 μM, reduces polymerase activity by 53.7% and 38.7%, while LMed 99 at 9 and 4.5 μM increased expression by 108.97% and 61.37%, respectively. Structure–activity relationship analysis highlighted that catechol groups and halogenation enhance antiviral potency. These findings suggest that LMed 93 and LMed 99 are promising coumarin-based scaffolds for developing new anti-Influenza A agents, also offering potential strategies for combating other RNA viruses.

papers.title: Analysis of Influenza A viruses using the resonant recognition model
papers.abstract: Bird flu (Avian influenza) and human flu are both caused by Influenza A viruses, but they differ significantly in their host adaptation, transmission and severity. Here, we have used the Resonant Recognition Model (RRM), which is innovative approach using knowledge from quantum physics, biochemistry and mathematics, capable to analyse interactions between proteins and their targets, including other proteins, DNA, RNA, or small molecules. Using the RRM model we have identified different characteristics for different types of flu viruses, and we have found that there are three groups of flu viruses with completely different interactions with host cells receptors. Such finding can provide explanation why different flu viruses can interact only with specific hosts and why there is extremely low cross infection between different species, in particular between birds and humans.
papers.journal: International Journal of Science and Research Archive

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现为为什么不同的流感病毒仅与特定的 宿主 相互作用以及为什么跨物种感染(特别是鸟类和人类之间)的感染率极低提供了新颖的解释。

papers.title: Aerosol transmission of infectious diseases in poultry: microbiology, pathogenesis, and control measures
papers.abstract: The expansion of intensive poultry production improves productivity but increases the risk of disease transmission. In poultry houses, infectious disease transmission occurs through direct and indirect routes, including surface contamination and vector-borne transmission. Typically, disease control in poultry mostly focuses on direct contact and management-related practices in poultry houses, but there is growing evidence highlighting the significance of the aerosol transmission route – an indirect route of pathogen spread that can impair production performance in poultry. High stocking density in poultry houses, inadequate ventilation, and poor biosecurity measures increase the risk of aerosolized transmission of bacterial, viral, and fungal pathogens. The efficiency of this route depends on particle size, humidity, temperature, and ventilation, which influence pathogen survival and exposure, and is further compounded by environmental stressors and the site of action within the animal’s respiratory system. Given that major pathogens, such as avian influenza virus, infectious bronchitis virus, avian orthoavulavirus 1, and Aspergillus spp., are usually transmitted via the aerosol route, it is essential for poultry farmers to adopt a range of mitigation strategies to achieve effective disease prevention and improve production output. As such, this review highlights the role of aerosol transmission in poultry health and management, focusing on microbiological aspects, pathogenesis, overall impact, and mitigation strategies. Also, this review aims to integrate current knowledge on aerosol characteristics with transmission dynamics and to provide insight into future research opportunities.

papers.abstract_original: The expansion of intensive poultry production improves productivity but increases the risk of disease transmission. In poultry houses, infectious disease transmission occurs through direct and indirect routes, including surface contamination and vector-borne transmission. Typically, disease control in poultry mostly focuses on direct contact and management-related practices in poultry houses, but there is growing evidence highlighting the significance of the aerosol transmission route – an indirect route of pathogen spread that can impair production performance in poultry. High stocking density in poultry houses, inadequate ventilation, and poor biosecurity measures increase the risk of aerosolized transmission of bacterial, viral, and fungal pathogens. The efficiency of this route depends on particle size, humidity, temperature, and ventilation, which influence pathogen survival and exposure, and is further compounded by environmental stressors and the site of action within the animal’s respiratory system. Given that major pathogens, such as avian influenza virus, infectious bronchitis virus, avian orthoavulavirus 1, and Aspergillus spp., are usually transmitted via the aerosol route, it is essential for poultry farmers to adopt a range of mitigation strategies to achieve effective disease prevention and improve production output. As such, this review highlights the role of aerosol transmission in poultry health and management, focusing on microbiological aspects, pathogenesis, overall impact, and mitigation strategies. Also, this review aims to integrate current knowledge on aerosol characteristics with transmission dynamics and to provide insight into future research opportunities.

papers.abstract_zh: 集约化家禽生产的扩大提高了生产率,但增加了疾病风险 传播。在禽舍中,传染病 传播 通过直接和间接途径发生,包括表面污染和 媒介 传播的 传播。通常,家禽疾病控制主要侧重于禽舍中的直接接触和管理相关做法,但越来越多的证据强调了气溶胶 传播 途径的重要性,这是一种病原体传播的间接途径,可能会损害家禽的生产性能。禽舍饲养密度高、通风不足和生物安全措施差会增加细菌、病毒和真菌病原体雾化 传播 的风险。该途径的效率取决于颗粒大小、湿度、温度和通风,这些因素会影响病原体的生存和暴露,并进一步受到环境压力源和动物呼吸系统内作用部位的影响。鉴于禽流感病毒、传染性支气管炎病毒、禽正鸟病毒1型和曲霉属等主要病原体通常通过气溶胶途径传播,家禽养殖户必须采取一系列缓解策略,以实现有效的疾病预防和提高产量。因此,本综述强调了气雾剂 传播 在家禽健康和管理中的作用,重点关注微生物方面、传播、总体影响和缓解策略。此外,本综述旨在将当前关于气溶胶特性的知识与 传播 动力学相结合,并提供对未来研究机会的见解。

papers.title: Twenty-Two Months of Syndromic Multiplex-PCR Testing for Acute Infections in a Southern Italian Hospital: Pathogen Epidemiology, Diagnostic Appropriateness and the Cost of Negative Results
papers.abstract: Syndromic multiplex-PCR panels deliver rapid, comprehensive detection of pathogens and resistance determinants in acute infections, but their unrestricted use can generate a high proportion of negative results with substantial economic and stewardship implications. We retrospectively analysed all BioFire FilmArray meningitis/encephalitis (ME), upper-respiratory (RP2.1), pneumonia (PN) and gastrointestinal (GI) determinations performed at the UOSD Microbiology and Virology of P.O. “Vito Fazzi”, ASL Lecce (Apulia, Italy) between 1 July 2024 and 30 April 2026. Repeat determinations from the same patient with the same panel were identified in the laboratory information system and removed before any analysis, so that each determination analysed corresponds to a distinct diagnostic episode. Across 5381 determinations (CNS, n = 761; upper respiratory, n = 2601; lower respiratory, n = 399; gastrointestinal, n = 1620), 59.3% were negative for every target, with a steep appropriateness gradient: 90.0% negativity for the ME panel and 77.1% for the gastrointestinal panel versus 44.2% for the upper-respiratory and 26.6% for the pneumonia panel. CNS positives were predominantly viral (75%), led by enterovirus; Streptococcus pneumoniae was the only consistent bacterial agent. Human rhinovirus/enterovirus dominated the respiratory ecology; influenza A was almost entirely H3 and H1N1pdm09, but 8.1% of influenza-A–positive specimens were equivocal or non-subtypeable and were never referred for sequencing, an avoidable surveillance blind spot for novel/zoonotic (avian) influenza. Pneumonia-panel resistance markers (mecA/C–MREJ, CTX-M, KPC, NDM) clustered in Enterobacterales co-infections. The gastrointestinal panel was dominated by diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes (chiefly EPEC and EAEC) and Clostridioides difficile toxin, its 77% negativity identifying a second over-utilised stream. We argue for CSF-pleocytosis gating, tiered/reflex respiratory algorithms, gastrointestinal-panel gating to community-onset diarrhoea, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the epidemiology, diagnostic appropriateness, and cost implications of syndromic multiplex-PCR testing for acute infections in a Southern Italian hospital, focusing on the high proportion of negative results and their economic impact.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis of all BioFire FilmArray meningitis/encephalitis (ME), upper-respiratory (RP2.1), pneumonia (PN), and gastrointestinal (GI) determinations performed at the UOSD Microbiology and Virology of P.O. 'Vito Fazzi', ASL Lecce (Apulia, Italy) between 1 July 2024 and 30 April 2026, with repeat determinations removed to ensure distinct diagnostic episodes.
analysis.methods: The study involved analysing 5381 determinations across four syndromic panels (CNS, upper respiratory, lower respiratory, gastrointestinal) to assess pathogen detection rates, diagnostic appropriateness, and resistance markers, with a focus on identifying avoidable surveillance blind spots like unsubtypeable influenza A.
analysis.main_results: Across 5381 determinations, 59.3% were negative for every target, with negativity rates varying by panel: 90.0% for ME, 77.1% for GI, 44.2% for upper-respiratory, and 26.6% for pneumonia. CNS positives were predominantly viral (75%), led by enterovirus, and Streptococcus pneumoniae was the only consistent bacterial agent. Influenza A was almost entirely H3 and H1N1pdm09, but 8.1% were equivocal or non-subtypeable and not referred for sequencing.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the high negativity rates as evidence of over-utilization of certain panels, particularly ME and GI, and highlighted the avoidable surveillance gap for unsubtypeable influenza A, which could miss novel or zoonotic strains. The novelty lies in the detailed epidemiological mapping of pathogen distribution and resistance patterns across multiple syndromic panels.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for targeted diagnostic strategies, such as CSF-pleocytosis gating for CNS testing, tiered respiratory algorithms, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A, to improve diagnostic appropriateness and surveillance for potential zoonotic influenza threats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and single-center setting, which may affect generalizability. However, the large sample size and comprehensive analysis provide moderate evidence strength for informing local diagnostic practices and surveillance protocols.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study evaluated syndromic multiplex-PCR testing over 22 months in a Southern Italian hospital, analysing 5381 determinations across CNS, respiratory, and gastrointestinal panels. A high proportion (59.3%) of results were negative, with rates varying by panel (90.0% for meningitis/encephalitis, 77.1% for gastrointestinal, 44.2% for upper-respiratory, and 26.6% for pneumonia). CNS positives were predominantly viral (75%), led by enterovirus, while Streptococcus pneumoniae was the only consistent bacterial agent. Influenza A was mostly H3 and H1N1pdm09, but 8.1% were unsubtypeable and not sequenced, representing a surveillance gap. The authors recommend targeted strategies like CSF-pleocytosis gating and mandatory sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A to improve diagnostic appropriateness and zoonotic surveillance.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the epidemiology, diagnostic appropriateness, and cost implications of syndromic multiplex-PCR testing for acute infections in a Southern Italian hospital, focusing on the high proportion of negative results and their economic impact.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis of all BioFire FilmArray meningitis/encephalitis (ME), upper-respiratory (RP2.1), pneumonia (PN), and gastrointestinal (GI) determinations performed at the UOSD Microbiology and Virology of P.O. 'Vito Fazzi', ASL Lecce (Apulia, Italy) between 1 July 2024 and 30 April 2026, with repeat determinations removed to ensure distinct diagnostic episodes.
analysis_en.methods: The study involved analysing 5381 determinations across four syndromic panels (CNS, upper respiratory, lower respiratory, gastrointestinal) to assess pathogen detection rates, diagnostic appropriateness, and resistance markers, with a focus on identifying avoidable surveillance blind spots like unsubtypeable influenza A.
analysis_en.main_results: Across 5381 determinations, 59.3% were negative for every target, with negativity rates varying by panel: 90.0% for ME, 77.1% for GI, 44.2% for upper-respiratory, and 26.6% for pneumonia. CNS positives were predominantly viral (75%), led by enterovirus, and Streptococcus pneumoniae was the only consistent bacterial agent. Influenza A was almost entirely H3 and H1N1pdm09, but 8.1% were equivocal or non-subtypeable and not referred for sequencing.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the high negativity rates as evidence of over-utilization of certain panels, particularly ME and GI, and highlighted the avoidable surveillance gap for unsubtypeable influenza A, which could miss novel or zoonotic strains. The novelty lies in the detailed epidemiological mapping of pathogen distribution and resistance patterns across multiple syndromic panels.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for targeted diagnostic strategies, such as CSF-pleocytosis gating for CNS testing, tiered respiratory algorithms, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A, to improve diagnostic appropriateness and surveillance for potential zoonotic influenza threats.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and single-center setting, which may affect generalizability. However, the large sample size and comprehensive analysis provide moderate evidence strength for informing local diagnostic practices and surveillance protocols.

papers.title_zh: 意大利南部一家医院对急性感染进行 22 个月的综合征多重 PCR 检测:病原体 流行病学、诊断适当性和阴性结果的成本
papers.source_body_en: Syndromic multiplex-PCR panels deliver rapid, comprehensive detection of pathogens and resistance determinants in acute infections, but their unrestricted use can generate a high proportion of negative results with substantial economic and stewardship implications. We retrospectively analysed all BioFire FilmArray meningitis/encephalitis (ME), upper-respiratory (RP2.1), pneumonia (PN) and gastrointestinal (GI) determinations performed at the UOSD Microbiology and Virology of P.O. “Vito Fazzi”, ASL Lecce (Apulia, Italy) between 1 July 2024 and 30 April 2026. Repeat determinations from the same patient with the same panel were identified in the laboratory information system and removed before any analysis, so that each determination analysed corresponds to a distinct diagnostic episode. Across 5381 determinations (CNS, n = 761; upper respiratory, n = 2601; lower respiratory, n = 399; gastrointestinal, n = 1620), 59.3% were negative for every target, with a steep appropriateness gradient: 90.0% negativity for the ME panel and 77.1% for the gastrointestinal panel versus 44.2% for the upper-respiratory and 26.6% for the pneumonia panel. CNS positives were predominantly viral (75%), led by enterovirus; Streptococcus pneumoniae was the only consistent bacterial agent. Human rhinovirus/enterovirus dominated the respiratory ecology; influenza A was almost entirely H3 and H1N1pdm09, but 8.1% of influenza-A–positive specimens were equivocal or non-subtypeable and were never referred for sequencing, an avoidable surveillance blind spot for novel/zoonotic (avian) influenza. Pneumonia-panel resistance markers (mecA/C–MREJ, CTX-M, KPC, NDM) clustered in Enterobacterales co-infections. The gastrointestinal panel was dominated by diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli pathotypes (chiefly EPEC and EAEC) and Clostridioides difficile toxin, its 77% negativity identifying a second over-utilised stream. We argue for CSF-pleocytosis gating, tiered/reflex respiratory algorithms, gastrointestinal-panel gating to community-onset diarrhoea, and mandatory reflex sequencing of unsubtypeable influenza A.
papers.abstract_zh: 综合征多重 PCR 检测板可以快速、全面地检测急性感染中的病原体和耐药性决定因素,但其不受限制的使用可能会产生很大比例的阴性结果,从而产生重大的经济和管理影响。我们回顾性分析了在 UOSD 微生物学和病毒学中心进行的所有 BioFire FilmArray 脑膜炎/脑炎 (ME)、上呼吸道 (RP2.1)、肺炎 (PN) 和胃肠道 (GI) 测定。“Vito Fazzi”,ASL 莱切(意大利普利亚),时间为 2024 年 7 月 1 日至 2026 年 4 月 30 日。实验室信息系统中识别出同一患者对同一组的重复测定结果,并在进行任何分析之前将其删除,以便分析的每个测定结果都对应于一个不同的诊断事件。在 5381 项测定中(中枢神经系统,n = 761;上呼吸道,n = 2601;下呼吸道,n = 399;胃肠道,n = 1620),每个目标都有 59.3% 呈阴性,适当性梯度陡峭:ME 组为 90.0%,胃肠组为 77.1%,而上呼吸道和胃肠道组为 44.2%。肺炎组为 26.6%。CNS 阳性主要是病毒(75%),其中以肠道病毒为主;肺炎链球菌是唯一一致的细菌病原体。人类鼻病毒/肠道病毒在呼吸道生态中占主导地位;甲型流感几乎完全是 H3 和 H1N1pdm09,但 8.1% 的甲型流感阳性标本是模棱两可或不可分型的,并且从未转介进行测序,这是新型/人畜共患(禽)流感的可避免的 监测 盲点。肺炎群体耐药标记(mecA/C-MREJ、CTX-M、KPC、NDM)聚集在肠杆菌科细菌合并感染中。胃肠道组以致泻性大肠杆菌致病型(主要是 EPEC 和 EAEC)和艰难梭菌毒素为主,其 77% 的阴性表明了第二个过度利用的流。我们主张脑脊液细胞增多门控、分层/反射呼吸算法、针对社区发病腹泻的胃肠道门控,以及对不可亚型甲型流感的强制反射测序。

papers.title: Önem Kazanan Solunum Yolu Virüsleri ve Güncel Gelişmeler
papers.abstract: Solunum yolu virüsleri son yıllarda artan tanı olanakları, yaşlı ve immün sistemi baskılanmış birey sayısının artması, değişen iklim koşulları, insan nüfusundaki artış, ulaşımın kolaylaşması ve bazı virüslerin pandemiye neden olabilme potansiyelleri nedeniyle giderek önem kazanmaktadır. Bu virüslerden özellikle respiratuar sinsityal virüs, influenza ve SARS-CoV-2 zatürreye neden olabilmekte, yaşlı ve bağışıklık sistemi zayıf hastalarda yaşamı tehdit edebilmektedir. Bunların dışında rinovirüs, adenovirüs, insan metapnömovirüsü giderek artan sıklıkta tanımlanan diğer solunum yolu virüslerindendir. Zoonotik kökenli virüslerin çeşitli mutasyonlarla insanda hastalık yapma özelliği kazanması ve salgınlara yol açmasını COVİD-19 ve Avian İnfluenza H5N1’de deneyimledik. Peki güncel tehditler ve gelişmeler neler? Bazı solunum yolu virüslerinden korunmak için aşı çalışmalarında ve tedavide umut verici gelişmeler mevcuttur. Yeni antiviral ilaçlar, monoklonal antikorlar ve aşı çalışmalarında durum ne? Bu genel derlemeyle önem kazanan solunum yolu virüslerinden bahsettik ve bu virüsler hakkındaki güncel gelişmeleri paylaştık.
papers.journal: Kahramanmaraş Sütçü İmam Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi Dergisi

analysis.summary_en: This review article discusses the growing importance of respiratory viruses in recent years due to various factors including increased diagnostic capabilities, aging populations, climate change, and pandemic potential. It highlights specific viruses such as respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, and SARS-CoV-2 that can cause life-threatening pneumonia in vulnerable populations, while also noting the increasing identification of other viruses like rhinovirus and adenovirus. The article references experiences with zoonotic viruses like COVID-19 and Avian Influenza H5N1, which have demonstrated the ability to mutate and cause human disease and pandemics. The review concludes by mentioning promising developments in vaccines and treatments for respiratory viruses, though specific details are not provided in this general overview.

papers.title: Flu Mutation Explorer: an Interactive Platform for Mapping Host Adaptation Mutations in Influenza A Viruses
papers.abstract: A rapid expansion of influenza A virus (IAV) genome sequencing has transformed global surveillance but has also created major challenges for interpreting the biological significance of viral mutations, particularly amino acid replacements associated with host adaptation. Resources have been created to support mutation annotation and phylogenetic analysis, but there is a need for a tool that integrates experimentally derived phenotypic evidence with evolutionary context in a framework suitable for users without prior training in bioinformatics. Here, we present the Flu Mutation Explorer, an interactive web application that combines large-scale influenza phylogenies with a manually curated database of reported mammalian adaptation mutations, to enable the exploration and interpretation of IAV genetic variation. The underlying database comprises over 1.5 million publicly available IAV sequences and over 1000 mutations associated with mammalian adaptation. The Flu Mutation Explorer enables users to query protein sequences, visualise amino acid distributions across viral lineages, examine host-specific conservation patterns, and identify adaptation mutation with links to supporting literature. We include case studies which demonstrate the platform's use in assessing amino acid conservation at sites of interest and in rapidly identifying candidate mammalian adaptation mutations during the ongoing H5N1 panzootic. By integrating genomic, phylogenetic, and functional information into an intuitive interface, the Flu Mutation Explorer lowers the barriers to interpreting influenza sequences for specialists and non-specialists alike.

analysis.time: Published on 2026-07-23. Event date not specified in the evidence.
analysis.location_and_population: Affected population: wild birds.
analysis.event: Confirmed detection of bird flu (HPAI) in individual wild birds in New Zealand. Reported by the Ministry for Primary Industries.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Cases: Individual wild birds. No specific case count, death count, or exposure count reported. Risk: Not explicitly stated in the evidence.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Public health response includes establishing an exotic pest and disease hotline (0800 80 99 66) and an online reporting portal (report.mpi.govt.nz) for reporting 3 or more sick or dead wild birds in a group. Guidance provided on limiting impact and being prepared for bird flu. No information on investigation, testing, isolation, contact tracing, or treatment status. Source limitation: Full original report body was reviewed.

analysis.brief_en: The New Zealand Ministry for Primary Industries has confirmed the detection of bird flu (HPAI) in individual wild birds within the country. In response, authorities have established a hotline and online reporting system for citizens to report groups of three or more sick or dead wild birds. The government is providing guidance to the public on how to limit the impact of the virus and be prepared for potential further spread. While the detection is confirmed in individual birds, no specific case numbers, deaths, or broader risk assessments have been disclosed. The focus remains on surveillance, reporting mechanisms, and public education to protect native species.

While the detection is confirmed in individual birds, no specific case numbers, deaths, or broader risk assessments have been disclosed. The focus remains on surveillance, reporting mechanisms, and public education to protect native species.

news.title_zh: 保护我们的本土物种免受高致病性禽流感(HPAI)的侵害 |新西兰政府 - 第一产业部
news.source_body_en: The New Zealand Ministry for Primary Industries has confirmed the detection of bird flu (HPAI) in individual wild birds within the country. In response, authorities have established a hotline and online reporting system for citizens to report groups of three or more sick or dead wild birds. The government is providing guidance to the public on how to limit the impact of the virus and be prepared for potential further spread. While the detection is confirmed in individual birds, no specific case numbers, deaths, or broader risk assessments have been disclosed. The focus remains on surveillance, reporting mechanisms, and public education to protect native species.
news.content_zh: 新西兰第一产业部已确认在该国境内个体 野生鸟类 中检测到禽流感 (HPAI)。为此,当局建立了热线电话和在线报告系统,供公民报告三人或三人以上患病或死亡的群体 野生鸟类。政府正在向公众提供有关如何限制病毒影响并为潜在的进一步传播做好准备的指导。虽然在个别鸟类中证实了这一检测,但尚未披露具体的病例数、死亡人数或更广泛的风险评估。重点仍然是 监测、报告机制和保护本土物种的公共教育。

news.title_zh: 禽流感 每周更新#1053:2026 年 7 月 18 日 - 世界卫生组织 (WHO)
news.source_body_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) Western Pacific Region has released its weekly update on avian influenza (Avian Influenza Weekly Update #1053) on 18 July 2026. This report focuses on avian influenza A viruses, which primarily spread among birds but can also infect humans through direct contact with infected poultry or contaminated environments. While these viruses do not currently transmit easily between people, their ongoing circulation in poultry poses a concern due to the potential for illness, death, and mutation. The update highlights recent developments in the regional response to avian influenza, emphasizing the importance of monitoring and preparedness.
news.content_zh: 世界卫生组织 (WHO) 西太平洋区域于 2026 年 7 月 18 日发布了 禽流感 每周更新(禽流感 每周更新#1053)。本报告重点关注 禽流感 A 病毒,该病毒主要在鸟类中传播,但也可以通过直接接触受感染的家禽或受污染的环境来感染人类。虽然这些病毒目前不易在人与人之间传播,但它们在家禽中的持续传播因其潜在的疾病、死亡和 突变 的可能性而引起关注。该更新强调了 禽流感 区域响应的最新进展,强调了监测和准备的重要性。

news.content_title: New Zealand detects first H5N1 bird flu case, starts vaccination of endangered species
news.content: WELLINGTON, July 15 (Reuters) - New Zealand reported its first case of the deadly H5N1 bird flu after a migratory seabird found on a beach near the capital, Wellington, tested positive, Biosecurity Minister Andrew Hoggard said on Wednesday. The case in a brown skua seabird comes after the virus was detected last month in Australia, the last continent to report the virus. The virulent H5 strain has spread through wild bird and mammal populations since 2021, killing millions and infecting poultry and dairy farms as well as some farmworkers. "There is no evidence of any mass mortality in wildlife or transmission between wild birds in New Zealand. There has been no detection in poultry," Hoggard said in a statement. Hoggard said New Zealand may see a similar pattern to cases reported in neighbouring Australia, where there have been 14 confirmed or presumed positive detections of H5 bird flu as of Wednesday. New Zealand has been preparing for the arrival of H5N1, working with the poultry industry to develop biosecurity and resilience plans. "We're going to be doing more surveillance, more testing, but by and large it's carrying on with the same work with the industry we've been doing so far," Hoggard said at a press conference. Many of New Zealand's endemic birds are unusually vulnerable because they evolved for millions of years without native land mammals, leaving many unique species, which are flightless, ground-nesting and poorly equipped to defend themselves against predators. That isolation made them unique but also left them highly exposed to habitat loss and introduced pests such as stoats, rats and feral cats. Many species are already endangered, putting them at great risk of extinction if the virus spreads rapidly. Health officials have started a vaccination programme for 300 core breeding birds from five of the country's most endangered species, including flightless takahe and kakapo. Hoggard said they had trialed the vaccine last year and had seen no adverse side effects but could not be certain how effective it was as the birds had not been exposed to the virus. Brett Gartrell, professor of wildlife health at Massey University, told Reuters he was worried that bird flu could push some of the country's critically endangered birds to extinction. "We are incredibly worried about New Zealand's biodiversity because our birds have never had to deal with anything like this before," Gartrell said. "If it spreads quickly in New Zealand, we could be in trouble," he said. (Reporting by Lucy Craymer in Wellington and Renju Jose in Sydney; Editing by Kate Mayberry, Sonali Paul and Lincoln Feast.)

selected_identity.page_title: New Zealand detects first H5N1 bird flu case, starts vaccination of endangered species

news.content_original: WELLINGTON, July 15 (Reuters) - New Zealand reported its first case of the deadly H5N1 bird flu after a migratory seabird found on a beach near the capital, Wellington, tested positive, Biosecurity Minister Andrew Hoggard said on Wednesday. The case in a brown skua seabird comes after the virus was detected last month in Australia, the last continent to report the virus. The virulent H5 strain has spread through wild bird and mammal populations since 2021, killing millions and infecting poultry and dairy farms as well as some farmworkers. "There is no evidence of any mass mortality in wildlife or transmission between wild birds in New Zealand. There has been no detection in poultry," Hoggard said in a statement. Hoggard said New Zealand may see a similar pattern to cases reported in neighbouring Australia, where there have been 14 confirmed or presumed positive detections of H5 bird flu as of Wednesday. New Zealand has been preparing for the arrival of H5N1, working with the poultry industry to develop biosecurity and resilience plans. "We're going to be doing more surveillance, more testing, but by and large it's carrying on with the same work with the industry we've been doing so far," Hoggard said at a press conference. Many of New Zealand's endemic birds are unusually vulnerable because they evolved for millions of years without native land mammals, leaving many unique species, which are flightless, ground-nesting and poorly equipped to defend themselves against predators. That isolation made them unique but also left them highly exposed to habitat loss and introduced pests such as stoats, rats and feral cats. Many species are already endangered, putting them at great risk of extinction if the virus spreads rapidly. Health officials have started a vaccination programme for 300 core breeding birds from five of the country's most endangered species, including flightless takahe and kakapo. Hoggard said they had trialed the vaccine last year and had seen no adverse side effects but could not be certain how effective it was as the birds had not been exposed to the virus. Brett Gartrell, professor of wildlife health at Massey University, told Reuters he was worried that bird flu could push some of the country's critically endangered birds to extinction. "We are incredibly worried about New Zealand's biodiversity because our birds have never had to deal with anything like this before," Gartrell said. "If it spreads quickly in New Zealand, we could be in trouble," he said. (Reporting by Lucy Craymer in Wellington and Renju Jose in Sydney; Editing by Kate Mayberry, Sonali Paul and Lincoln Feast.)

news.content_title: # H5N1 has arrived: What the end of Australia's Bird Flu freedom means for poultry producers | Lockton
news.content: ARTICLES / JULY 21, 2026 # H5N1 has arrived: What the end of Australia's Bird Flu freedom means for poultry producers Until June 2026, Australia held a distinction no other continent could claim: complete freedom from the H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b strain of avian influenza that has devastated poultry flocks across Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas since 2021. That distinction has now ended. On 20 June 2026, a vagrant migratory seabird found in Cape Le Grand National Park on Western Australia's southern coast tested positive for high pathogenicity H5N1. As at 15 July 2026, Australia has 14 confirmed or presumed positive detections in wild birds: eight in Western Australia, five in South Australia and one in New South Wales, most recently a giant petrel found near Hawks Nest. All detections to date are in wild seabirds. There is no evidence of infection in commercial poultry, no evidence of mass mortality events and currently no trade restrictions on Australian poultry or poultry product exports. For poultry producers, this is not cause for panic, but it is a genuine inflection point. Australia's biosecurity system has successfully contained every prior HPAI incursion, including the H7N3 and H7N9 outbreaks that hit eight Victorian properties in 2024 and the H7N8 outbreak that affected four Victorian properties in early 2025. Both were eradicated within months. H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, however, behaves differently to the H7 strains Australia has dealt with before. Globally, it has proven more transmissible in wild bird populations, more persistent, and more capable of spilling into mammals. The World Organisation for Animal Health recorded more than 2,000 HPAI outbreaks across 64 countries between 2025 and 2026, resulting in the loss or culling of over 140 million birds. Why this changes the risk calculation The reservoir is now local Wild seabirds carrying the virus are established along Australia's southern and western coastlines. Migratory bird pathways and proximity to wetlands, estuaries and coastal roosting sites are now a live exposure factor for any producer, not a theoretical one. 2. Industry is already responding. Inghams, Australia's largest poultry producer, has locked down non-essential access to its Western Australian operations and sought a regional housing order to bring free-range flocks indoors. Producers in WA and SA in particular should expect this pattern to spread as detections continue. 3. Detection does not equal containment cost. A single infected commercial shed can trigger movement restrictions, culling and quarantine well beyond that property, affecting neighbouring producers, hatcheries, transport contractors and processors who never had a sick bird on site. 4. Trade sensitivity is heightened. Australia's clean status has long been a competitive advantage in export markets. The first confirmed poultry infection, even if swiftly contained, is likely to trigger a period of heightened scrutiny from trading partners and potential short-term restrictions while status is reassessed. What producers should be doing now Tighten biosecurity to outbreak-ready standard Vehicle disinfection points, restricted shed access, dedicated PPE and strict control of movement between sites are no longer precautionary extras. Where feasible, consider housing orders or netting for free-range and outdoor-access flocks, particularly in WA, SA and coastal NSW. 2. Deter and monitor wild bird contact. Covered feed and water sources, netting over outdoor ranges and active discouragement of wild waterfowl on or near production sites reduce the single biggest transmission pathway. 3. Report early, without exception. Any unusual mortality, respiratory signs or drop in egg production should go straight to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline (1800 675 888). Early detection is the difference between a contained incident and a prolonged one. 4. Review insurance now, not after a detection. Livestock mortality and business interruption capacity for avian influenza contracts sharply once an outbreak reaches commercial poultry. Cover secured ahead of a confirmed infection is materially easier to place and typically better priced than cover sought during an active event. 5. Understand what government compensation does and does not cover. Compensation schemes generally address the direct cost of culling and disposal. They do not typically extend to lost production, lost contracts, restocking delays, or the broader revenue interruption that follows a quarantine period. That gap is where a well-structured business interruption policy can do its work. The people risk: managing stress in your own workforce The financial and operational consequences of an outbreak are well understood. The impact on the people who have to manage it is less often discussed and deserves equal weight in planning. Mass depopulation is traumatic work. Overseas experience from major HPAI and FMD events consistently shows elevated rates of acute stress, sleep disturbance and longer-term psychological impact among the staff, contract cullers and vets directly involved in culling and disposal. This is not a fringe consideration. It is a predictable outcome of the work itself. 2. Owner-operators carry a compounding load. Financial uncertainty while awaiting compensation, regulatory scrutiny, movement restrictions that cut off normal social contact, and public or media attention can pile on the practical demands of running an outbreak response. Family-run operations, in particular, have no separation between business and personal stress. 3. This now sits within your WHS duty of care. Psychosocial hazards, including exposure to traumatic events and high job demand with low support, are explicitly covered under Australia's model WHS laws. An outbreak response plan that addresses biosecurity and logistics but not the psychosocial exposure of the people executing it is incomplete from a compliance standpoint, not just a well-being one. 4. Build workforce support into the response plan itself, not as an afterthought. Practical measures can include rotating staff involved in culling and disposal to limit cumulative exposure, engaging EAP or trained counselling support ahead of and during the event rather than only after, keeping communication with staff clear and honest to reduce uncertainty-driven anxiety, and involving HR or WHS leads in outbreak planning alongside the biosecurity and insurance teams. 5. Check whether your cover reflects this. Business Interruption cover can also do double duty here: removing financial uncertainty as a live variable during an active event reduces one of the biggest stressors for owner-operators. The bottom line Australia's poultry sector has a strong track record of containing and eradicating avian influenza outbreaks. What has changed is the nature of the threat. For the first time, H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has been detected in Australia's wild bird population, bringing a risk profile that is more persistent, more unpredictable and potentially more disruptive than previous HPAI incursions. While there is currently no evidence of infection in commercial poultry, producers now face a different operating environment. The challenge is no longer simply preventing an outbreak on-site. It is understanding how a detection on a neighbouring property, within a nearby wild bird colony, or elsewhere in the supply chain could affect operations, workforce wellbeing, contractual obligations and financial performance. The businesses best positioned to respond will likely be those that act before a commercial detection occurs. That means reviewing biosecurity measures, testing outbreak response plans, addressing workforce and psychosocial risks, and ensuring insurance and business continuity arrangements reflect the realities of a prolonged disruption. In a landscape where the risk has changed, preparedness remains one or the most effective forms of protection. Don't wait until capacity tightens Following a confirmed commercial outbreak, insurance availability and underwriting appetite can change quickly. Now is the time to review your livestock mortality, business interruption and broader risk management arrangements. Understand what government compensation does and does not cover. Compensation schemes generally address the direct cost of culling and disposal. They do not typically extend to lost production, lost contracts, restocking delays, or the broader revenue interruption that follows a quarantine period. That gap is where a well-structured business interruption policy can do its work. The people risk: managing stress in your own workforce The financial and operational consequences of an outbreak are well understood. The impact on the people who have to manage it is less often discussed and deserves equal weight in planning. Mass depopulation is traumatic work. Overseas experience from major HPAI and FMD events consistently shows elevated rates of acute stress, sleep disturbance and longer-term psychological impact among the staff, contract cullers and vets directly involved in culling and disposal. This is not a fringe consideration. It is a predictable outcome of the work itself. 2. Owner-operators carry a compounding load. Financial uncertainty while awaiting compensation, regulatory scrutiny, movement restrictions that cut off normal social contact, and public or media attention can pile on the practical demands of running an outbreak response. Family-run operations, in particular, have no separation between business and personal stress. 3. This now sits within your WHS duty of care. Psychosocial hazards, including exposure to traumatic events and high job demand with low support, are explicitly covered under Australia's model WHS laws. An outbreak response plan that addresses biosecurity and logistics but not the psychosocial exposure of the people executing it is incomplete from a compliance standpoint, not just a well-being one. 4. Build workforce support into the response plan itself, not as an afterthought. Practical measures can include rotating staff involved in culling and disposal to limit cumulative exposure, engaging EAP or trained counselling support ahead of and during the event rather than only after, keeping communication with staff clear and honest to reduce uncertainty-driven anxiety, and involving HR or WHS leads in outbreak planning alongside the biosecurity and insurance teams. 5. Check whether your cover reflects this. Business Interruption cover can also do double duty here: removing financial uncertainty as a live variable during an active event reduces one of the biggest stressors for owner-operators. The bottom line Australia's poultry sector has a strong track record of containing and eradicating avian influenza outbreaks. What has changed is the nature of the threat. For the first time, H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b has been detected in Australia's wild bird population, bringing a risk profile that is more persistent, more unpredictable and potentially more disruptive than previous HPAI incursions. While there is currently no evidence of infection in commercial poultry, producers now face a different operating environment. The challenge is no longer simply preventing an outbreak on-site. It is understanding how a detection on a neighbouring property, within a nearby wild bird colony, or elsewhere in the supply chain could affect operations, workforce wellbeing, contractual obligations and financial performance. The businesses best positioned to respond will likely be those that act before a commercial detection occurs. That means reviewing biosecurity measures, testing outbreak response plans, addressing workforce and psychosocial risks, and ensuring insurance and business continuity arrangements reflect the realities of a prolonged disruption. In a landscape where the risk has changed, preparedness remains one or the most effective forms of protection. Don't wait until capacity tightens Following a confirmed commercial outbreak, insurance availability and underwriting appetite can change quickly. Now is the time to review your livestock mortality, business interruption and broader risk management arrangements. analysis.event: Confirmed detection of highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b in wild seabirds in Australia, ending the country's freedom from this strain. Reported by official sources and industry stakeholders. Event is confirmed and ongoing.

No commercial poultry infections, mass mortality events, or trade restrictions reported. Global context: Over 2,000 HPAI outbreaks in 64 countries (2025-2026), with 140+ million birds lost. analysis.brief_en: Australia has lost its status as free from H5N1 avian influenza, with the first confirmed detection of highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b in wild seabirds reported on 20 June 2026. As of 15 July, 14 cases have been identified across Western Australia, South Australia, and New South Wales, all in wild birds with no commercial poultry infections to date. This marks a significant shift, as the strain is more transmissible and persistent than previous HPAI incursions Australia has successfully contained. While no trade restrictions are currently in place, the established wild bird reservoir elevates exposure risks for poultry producers. Industry responses include enhanced biosecurity measures, with companies like Inghams implementing lockdowns and seeking housing orders for flocks. Authorities emphasize early reporting via the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline and stress the importance of business continuity planning, as government compensation does not cover lost production or broader revenue impacts. The psychosocial toll on outbreak responders is also noted as a critical consideration under workplace safety obligations.
