READ SUMMARY SUBSCRIBE RECEIVE IN PAPER OTHER EDITIONS Back 21 Jul 2026 Study links poultry networks to H9N2 prevalence in Vietnam Low pathogenicity avian influenza A subtype H9N2 viruses are endemic in Vietnam. Arief Fachrudin aviNews Asia SAVE IN THE LIBRARY PDF FILE Animal Health & PathologyResearchAvian influenzaH9n2 Poultry production and distribution network configurations, including the origins of supplying farms, influence H9N2 avian influenza virus prevalence and thus human exposure risk, results from a study indicated. The study was performed by Dr Mathew Hennessey of the Royal Veterinary College in London, UK and his team of researchers. Figure 1. Geographic area and sites for study of avian influenza virus A(H9N2) prevalence across chicken production and distribution networks, Bac Giang, Hanoi, Hai Duong, and Quang Ninh Provinces, Vietnam, March 2021–March 2022. The 4 study provinces and the individual sites (farms and distribution facilities) are shown alongside the detection of avian influenza viruses (contaminated defined as >1 positive sample; noncontaminated defined as all samples testing negative) and the spatiotemporal cluster of contaminated farms. The 2 other farms that appear located in the cluster were not sampled during the temporal window. A cross-sectional study in northern Vietnam Their research paper explained that high-pathogenicity avian influenza A subtype H5N1 viruses of the Goose/Guangdong/1/96 lineage and low pathogenicity avian influenza A subtype H9N2 viruses are endemic in Southeast Asia, including Vietnam. Both subtypes affect poultry production and pose zoonotic risks directly and through their involvement in the generation of novel virus reassortments. In Vietnam, the subtypes are frequently detected in live bird markets, and higher prevalence is associated with practices such as mixing poultry from multiple sources. Figure 2. Time-scaled phylogenies of hemagglutinin sampled avian influenza virus A(H9N2) virus genomes in study of H9N2 virus prevalence across chicken production and distribution networks, Bac Giang, Hanoi, Hai Duong, and Quang Ninh Provinces, Vietnam, March 2021–March 2022. Tree tips are labeled by the unique sampled site identification; red text indicates sequences from 3 farms in the spatiotemporal cluster. Branches are colored by posterior support, and horizontal node bars represent 95% highest posterior density intervals of node ages. Heatmaps indicate province, site type, and chicken type of each sequence. C, chicken type; P, province; S, site type.Continue after advertising. However, that finding should be interpreted cautiously because farms and the markets they supply have limited prevalence data, and the focus on markets has diverted attention from larger slaughter facilities despite those facilities playing a key role in poultry distribution, the researchers stated. Together, those gaps constrain understanding of avian influenza virus (AIV) transmission risk along the production and distribution network (PDN) through which poultry are raised, traded, and consumed. The researchers conducted a cross-sectional study in northern Vietnam to assess avian influenza A(H5N1) and A(H9N2) prevalence in chickens, determine how AIV prevalence varied between farms and the different distribution facility types, and examine how viral genetic diversity was structured along the PDN. Figure 3. Time-scaled phylogenies of neuraminidase of sampled avian influenza virus A(H9N2) virus genomes in study of H9N2 virus prevalence across chicken production and distribution networks, Bac Giang, Hanoi, Hai Duong, and Quang Ninh Provinces, Vietnam, March 2021–March 2022. Tree tips are labeled by the unique sampled site identification; red text indicates sequences from 3 farms in the spatiotemporal cluster. Branches are colored by posterior support, and horizontal node bars represent 95% highest posterior density intervals of node ages. Heatmaps indicate province, site type, and chicken type of each sequence. C, chicken type; P, province; S site type. Findings from the study The researchers found that poultry production and distribution network configurations, including the origins of supplying farms, influence H9N2 virus prevalence and thus human exposure risk. The pattern of viral circulation amplification along the PDN is consistent with studies in southern Vietnam and Bangladesh and probably reflects trading conditions. For example, birds are mixed from multiple sources and experience lengthy, stressful transportation (for example: crowding and lack of sustenance), creating opportunities for virus exposure and transmission en route; that finding was supported by the improved model fit when they included supplying areas, suggesting that procurement and distribution practices influence viral prevalence at distribution facilities. High viral prevalence in slaughter points and retail markets probably reflects sourcing involving multiple suppliers, including wholesale markets, indicating that chickens spent longer in the PDN before sampling. The lack of geographic structure in AIV genetic diversity further points to extensive viral mixing among poultry populations. Control and surveillance efforts should therefore address the entire poultry PDN. The Vietnam Avian and Human Influenza Preparedness program has prioritized upgrading wholesale markets and industrial slaughterhouses and promoting their use. Although low prevalence in such facilities supports this focus, slaughterhouses remain underused, and informal slaughter points are still preferred. Surveillance and risk mitigation strategies must also target the numerous distribution facilities in Vietnam that are small and informal but widely used. Read full paper of the study here. Arief Fachrudin aviNews Asia SAVE IN THE LIBRARY PDF FILE Animal Health & PathologyResearchAvian influenzaH9n2 Poultry production and distribution network configurations, including the origins of supplying farms, influence H9N2 avian influenza virus prevalence and thus human exposure risk, results from a study indicated. The study was performed by Dr Mathew Hennessey of the Royal Veterinary College in London, UK and his team of researchers. Figure 1. Geographic area and sites for study of avian influenza virus A(H9N2) prevalence across chicken production and distribution networks, Bac Giang, Hanoi, Hai Duong, and Quang Ninh Provinces, Vietnam, March 2021–March 2022. The 4 study provinces and the individual sites (farms and distribution facilities) are shown alongside the detection of avian influenza viruses (contaminated defined as >1 positive sample; noncontaminated defined as all samples testing negative) and the spatiotemporal cluster of contaminated farms. The 2 other farms that appear located in the cluster were not sampled during the temporal window. A cross-sectional study in northern Vietnam Their research paper explained that high-pathogenicity avian influenza A subtype H5N1 viruses of the Goose/Guangdong/1/96 lineage and low pathogenicity avian influenza A subtype H9N2 viruses are endemic in Southeast Asia, including Vietnam. Both subtypes affect poultry production and pose zoonotic risks directly and through their involvement in the generation of novel virus reassortments. In Vietnam, the subtypes are frequently detected in live bird markets, and higher prevalence is associated with practices such as mixing poultry from multiple sources. Figure 2. Time-scaled phylogenies of hemagglutinin sampled avian influenza virus A(H9N2) virus genomes in study of H9N2 virus prevalence across chicken production and distribution networks, Bac Giang, Hanoi, Hai Duong, and Quang Ninh Provinces, Vietnam, March 2021–March 2022. Tree tips are labeled by the unique sampled site identification; red text indicates sequences from 3 farms in the spatiotemporal cluster. Branches are colored by posterior support, and horizontal node bars represent 95% highest posterior density intervals of node ages. Heatmaps indicate province, site type, and chicken type of each sequence. C, chicken type; P, province; S, site type.Continue after advertising. However, that finding should be interpreted cautiously because farms and the markets they supply have limited prevalence data, and the focus on markets has diverted attention from larger slaughter facilities despite those facilities playing a key role in poultry distribution, the researchers stated. Together, those gaps constrain understanding of avian influenza virus (AIV) transmission risk along the production and distribution network (PDN) through which poultry are raised, traded, and consumed. The researchers conducted a cross-sectional study in northern Vietnam to assess avian influenza A(H5N1) and A(H9N2) prevalence in chickens, determine how AIV prevalence varied between farms and the different distribution facility types, and examine how viral genetic diversity was structured along the PDN. Figure 3. Time-scaled phylogenies of neuraminidase of sampled avian influenza virus A(H9N2) virus genomes in study of H9N2 virus prevalence across chicken production and distribution networks, Bac Giang, Hanoi, Hai Duong, and Quang Ninh Provinces, Vietnam, March 2021–March 2022. Tree tips are labeled by the unique sampled site identification; red text indicates sequences from 3 farms in the spatiotemporal cluster. Branches are colored by posterior support, and horizontal node bars represent 95% highest posterior density intervals of node ages. Heatmaps indicate province, site type, and chicken type of each sequence. C, chicken type; P, province; S site type. Findings from the study The researchers found that poultry production and distribution network configurations, including the origins of supplying farms, influence H9N2 virus prevalence and thus human exposure risk. The pattern of viral circulation amplification along the PDN is consistent with studies in southern Vietnam and Bangladesh and probably reflects trading conditions. For example, birds are mixed from multiple sources and experience lengthy, stressful transportation (for example: crowding and lack of sustenance), creating opportunities for virus exposure and transmission en route; that finding was supported by the improved model fit when they included supplying areas, suggesting that procurement and distribution practices influence viral prevalence at distribution facilities. High viral prevalence in slaughter points and retail markets probably reflects sourcing involving multiple suppliers, including wholesale markets, indicating that chickens spent longer in the PDN before sampling. The lack of geographic structure in AIV genetic diversity further points to extensive viral mixing among poultry populations. Control and surveillance efforts should therefore address the entire poultry PDN. The Vietnam Avian and Human Influenza Preparedness program has prioritized upgrading wholesale markets and industrial slaughterhouses and promoting their use. Although low prevalence in such facilities supports this focus, slaughterhouses remain underused, and informal slaughter points are still preferred. Surveillance and risk mitigation strategies must also target the numerous distribution facilities in Vietnam that are small and informal but widely used. Read full paper of the study here. analysis.brief_en: A study by Dr. Mathew Hennessey and his team from the Royal Veterinary College, London, reveals that poultry production and distribution network configurations in northern Vietnam significantly influence H9N2 avian influenza virus prevalence and human exposure risk. Conducted from March 2021 to March 2022 across Bac Giang, Hanoi, Hai Duong, and Quang Ninh Provinces, the research found that practices like mixing poultry from multiple sources and stressful transportation conditions amplify viral circulation along the production and distribution network (PDN). The endemic H9N2 viruses pose direct zoonotic risks and contribute to novel virus reassortments. While Vietnam's Avian and Human Influenza Preparedness program focuses on upgrading wholesale markets and industrial slaughterhouses, informal slaughter points remain widely used, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance and risk mitigation strategies for small, informal distribution facilities.

news.content: FFAR rapid funding to explore disease-resistant poultry for avian influenza control News News | Jul 21, 2026 Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research DAVIS, Calif. — Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) continues to cause major losses for poultry farms around the world, killing millions of commercial and wild birds, disrupting food supplies, and increasing concerns on transmission among multiple animal species. In response, the Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research and the University of California, Davis, are investing $299,938 in a Rapid Outcomes from Agricultural Research grant to identify and harness natural disease resistance in chickens as a new tool to combat avian influenza. Current approaches, including vaccines, can help manage outbreaks. But they face challenges related to availability, speed of deployment and long-term effectiveness. This research project will explore whether some chickens naturally resist infection better than others and how that resistance could strengthen commercial poultry flocks. “Producers need tools to mitigate their losses, and FFAR’s rapid funding is helping to develop the solutions they need,” said Dr. Miriam Martin LeValley, FFAR scientific program manager. “Identifying whether some chickens naturally resist infection could help us craft an effective long-term HPAI response.” FAYOUMI CHICKENS Researchers led by Dr. Huaijun Zhou, Chancellor’s leadership professor and Dr. Rodrigo Gallardo, poultry virologist, at the University of California, Davis, will study the Fayoumi breed, a heritage chicken known for its hardiness and disease resistance. By using eggs containing a developing chick embryo — a safe and efficient research model — the team will compare how Fayoumi, broiler and layer chickens respond to highly pathogenic avian influenza. The researchers will evaluate survival and virus levels across the different breeds. They will also characterize immune responses to infection to identify the genes and biological pathways associated with disease resistance. “HPAI continues to challenge poultry production worldwide, highlighting the need for innovative and sustainable solutions,” said Dr. Zhou. “By identifying the genetic and immune factors that contribute to natural disease resistance, this research could help pave the way for more resilient poultry populations and improved long-term disease control.” Findings from this project could support future breeding programs aimed at enhancing natural resistance to disease in commercial poultry populations. More resilient flocks could reduce economic losses, lessen reliance on emergency disease control measures and strengthen the stability and sustainability of the U.S. food supply. ROAR rapidly funds research and outreach in response to emerging or unanticipated threats to the U.S. food supply or agricultural systems. analysis.brief_en: The Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research (FFAR) and University of California, Davis have announced a $299,938 Rapid Outcomes from Agricultural Research (ROAR) grant to combat highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) by exploring natural disease resistance in poultry. This research, led by Dr. Huaijun Zhou and Dr. Rodrigo Gallardo, will focus on Fayoumi chickens, a heritage breed known for hardiness. Using chick embryos as a research model, the team will compare survival rates, virus levels, and immune responses among Fayoumi, broiler, and layer chickens. The goal is to identify genetic and biological factors associated with disease resistance to develop more resilient commercial poultry populations. This initiative addresses global HPAI outbreaks that have caused significant economic losses and disrupted food supplies, offering a potential long-term solution beyond current control measures like vaccines.

H5N1 and H7N9 infections and find promising targets for new therapies to protect flocks.Foundation for Food & Agriculture ResearchJuly 22, 2026schedule2 Min ReadU.S. Department of AgricultureHighly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) continues to threaten the U.S. poultry industry, causing billions of dollars in economic losses while disrupting food production and increasing costs for farmers and consumers.The Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research (FFAR), Iowa State University and the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organization (CSIRO) are investing $300,000 through the Rapid Outcomes from Agricultural Research (ROAR) program to identify genetic factors in birds that are relevant in the host response against H5N1 and H7N9 avian influenza viruses. This research aims to illuminate pathways to modulate the expression of specific host genes to mitigate the avian influenza burden.Although biosecurity measures remain the primary means of combating avian influenza, developments since 2022 demonstrate the need for new approaches. There is an increasing request for the deployment of vaccines; however, concerns remain about vaccine effectiveness and virus evolution.Related:New pathway for B cell development in chickens discovered“We must explore every possible tool in the toolbox to protect producers and their flocks. Unlocking genetic mechanisms that naturally allow birds to resist infection could pave the way for innovative approaches that better protect flocks, strengthen food security and protect producers’ profitability,” said Miriam Martin LeValley, Ph.D., FFAR scientific program manager.This research is identifying genes involved in birds’ immune responses that influence how the virus infects and replicates. Understanding the role of genetics could better inform treatment protocols, improve disease resistance and strengthen future disease prevention strategies.Led by Dr. Joaquin Caceres, assistant professor in the Department of Veterinary Microbiology and Preventive Medicine, College of Veterinary Medicine, at Iowa State University, the multidisciplinary research team is using advanced genomic tools and novel laboratory models to better understand how birds respond to H5N1 and H7N9 infections.The project is identifying promising genetic targets for new therapies, supporting the development of next-generation vaccines and laying the foundation for breeding poultry with greater natural resistance to avian influenza.This FFAR-funded research supports the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s research priority on Increasing Profitability of Farmers and Ranchers. This research aims to provide alternative tools for protecting poultry flocks in the near- and long-term future.FFAR’s ROAR program rapidly funds research and outreach in response to emerging or unanticipated threats to the U.S. food supply or agricultural systems.Related:Social dynamics play key role in broiler breeder reproductive success“Influenza viruses, like any other virus, are obligate intracellular parasites. Therefore, if we modify the host environment, that must have consequences for the virus,” said Dr. Caceres. “Most current mitigation efforts against influenza are against the virus itself, but the virus has evolved multiple elegant ways to circumvent these strategies. Host-directed interventions may offer a more durable approach because host genetic pathways are substantially more stable than the viral genome.”.FFAR builds public-private partnerships to fund bold research addressing big food and agriculture challenges, matching federal funding from Congress with private funding. FFAR was established in the 2014 Farm Bill to increase public agriculture research investments, fill knowledge gaps and complement USDA’s research agenda. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The research is in progress, using advanced genomic tools and novel laboratory models to understand bird responses to H5N1 and H7N9 infections. It supports the USDA's research priority on increasing farmer profitability and aims to provide alternative tools for protecting poultry flocks in the near and long term. No current outbreak or immediate response is described; the focus is on future prevention strategies.

analysis.brief_en: The Foundation for Food and Agriculture Research (FFAR), Iowa State University, and CSIRO have launched a $300,000 research project to identify genetic factors in birds that confer immunity to H5N1 and H7N9 avian influenza viruses. This initiative, funded through the ROAR program, aims to discover genetic targets for new therapies and develop poultry with enhanced natural resistance. The research addresses the significant economic and food security threats posed by HPAI, which has cost the U.S. poultry industry billions in losses. While biosecurity remains the primary defense, the project explores host-directed interventions as a more durable alternative to current virus-focused strategies. Led by Dr. Joaquin Caceres at Iowa State, the team uses advanced genomic tools to understand avian immune responses, supporting the USDA's goal of improving farmer profitability and food system resilience.

news.content: The top news stories in medicine today. HHS cited concerns about the study’s methodology; the report found vaccines cut ED visits and hospitalizations by approximately half this past winter. A report showing the effectiveness of COVID-19 vaccines has been blocked from publication in the CDC's Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report (MMWR). "The manuscript was not accepted for publication" due to concerns about the "methodological approach estimating vaccine effectiveness," said HHS spokesman Andrew Nixon. The MMWR is one of the CDC's primary vehicles for publishing public health findings and is closely watched by physicians, researchers and state health officials. The decision comes under the leadership of HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., whose vaccine advisory panel last September scrapped a broad recommendation for COVID shots — a move since temporarily blocked by a federal court. Had it been published, the report would have shown that the vaccines reduced emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations among healthy adults by approximately ‌half this ⁠past winter, as reported by Reuters . Adam Brosius was ordered to pay $33 million in restitution and forfeit $27 million. A former New Jersey pharmacy president has been sentenced to 24 months in prison for his role in a $33 million health care fraud and kickback scheme involving medically unnecessary compounded medications including scar creams, pain creams, migraine medication and vitamins. Adam Brosius, 61, of Delray Beach, Florida, served as director of business development and later president of Main Avenue Pharmacy, a mail-order pharmacy in Clifton, New Jersey, which from 2014 through 2016 distributed pre-printed prescription pads featuring high-reimbursement compounded drug formulas to marketers nationwide. Those marketers passed the pads to telemedicine companies and physicians under financial arrangements, and Main Avenue paid kickbacks based on prescription volume and reimbursement amounts after billing Medicare, TRICARE and commercial insurers. The pharmacy collected approximately $33 million in reimbursements for compounded medications, more than $5.8 million of which came from TRICARE. In addition to his prison term, Brosius was ordered to pay $33 million in restitution and forfeit $27 million. The mRNA-1018 vaccine is the first pandemic bird flu shot made with mRNA technology to reach late-stage trials. Moderna has begun a late-stage trial of its experimental bird flu vaccine, mRNA-1018, enrolling approximately 4,000 healthy adults in the United States and United Kingdom — the first time an mRNA-based pandemic bird flu vaccine has reached this stage of testing. The trial is backed by a $54 million investment from the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI), which stepped in after HHS Kennedy canceled more than $700 million in U.S. government contracts with Moderna for bird flu vaccine development last May. If approved and a flu pandemic is declared, Moderna said it would reserve 20% of its manufacturing capacity for supply to low- and middle-income countries at affordable prices. The company said any regulatory filing for mRNA-1018 would also be supported by data from its seasonal flu vaccine candidate, mRNA-1010, currently under review in the U.S., European Union, Canada and Australia. Nihar R. Desai, MD, MPH; Martha Gulati, MD, MS, FACC, FAHA, MASPC, FESC, FSCCT (hon), FRCP Edin

analysis.brief_en: New Zealand's Ministry of Primary Industries (MPI) reported a surge in bird flu notifications after detecting the H5N1 strain in two wild birds. On Saturday alone, MPI received 157 reports of dead or unwell birds. Chief veterinary officer Mary van Andel confirmed the H5N1 detection but emphasized no new human cases have been confirmed. The surge in reports highlights increased public vigilance following the initial detection. MPI continues to monitor the situation and investigate the source of the infections. The public is urged to report any unusual bird mortality to authorities as the investigation progresses.

The surge in reports highlights increased public vigilance following the initial detection. MPI continues to monitor the situation and investigate the source of the infections. The public is urged to report any unusual bird mortality to authorities as the investigation progresses.

news.content_title: Bird flu warning prevents world pandemic
news.content: Bird flu warning prevents world pandemic UN official says early warning on possible virus mutation generated right response in governments, preventing an immediate pandemic. He makes an appeal for Indonesia and Africa. October 25, 2006 New York (AsiaNews/Agencies)  More than 30 countries have recorded bird flu outbreaks. Although the number of H5N1 virus-related deaths is rising, the United Nations is satisfied that a quick response by governments last year prevented a pandemic, said David Nabarro, a senior UN health coordinator. In February Mr Nabarro warned countries against the possibility of person-to-person transmission or an imminent pandemic because of a possible mutation in the H5N1 virus. Except for the Americas, the virus has infected birds around the world and led to the cullying of millions of poultry, geese and other birds. "In 2006, we did see more than 30 countries reporting outbreaks," Nabarro said. "Unfortunately, the virus continues to affect humanswith 256 people known to be affected and 151 dying" since 2003. The monthly trend in bird flu-related human deaths is upward, especially because of Indonesia, the most affected country. The UN official has called for stepped up economic and organisational assistance, especially for Indonesia and Africa. In his view, the H5N1 avian influenza virus should remain a major issue for most of the world for at least five years, and perhaps 10 years. One key to tackling the bird flu is to change poultry rearing practices. Bird flu seems to be spread by a combination of wild birds that migrate and trade in infected birds. Many experts also believe it will take five to 10 years to change poultry rearing practices, especially in countries where poultry is plentiful and birds are kept in the backyard

analysis.brief_en: A UN official has confirmed that early warnings and government responses in 2006 prevented an immediate pandemic of H5N1 avian influenza (bird flu). More than 30 countries reported outbreaks, with 256 human cases and 151 deaths since 2003, primarily in Indonesia. The virus has infected birds globally (except the Americas), leading to the culling of millions of poultry. Despite the prevention of an immediate pandemic, the UN warns that H5N1 remains a major global threat for at least 5-10 years, requiring sustained economic and organizational assistance, particularly for Indonesia and Africa. Key to controlling the outbreak is changing poultry rearing practices, which experts believe will take 5-10 years to implement effectively.

analysis.brief_en: The Cook Islands Ministry of Agriculture has activated a precautionary alert following the detection of H5N1 bird flu in New Zealand. While no cases have been confirmed in the Cook Islands, the ministry is monitoring the situation closely and may restrict poultry imports from New Zealand if the virus is found in domestic flocks. The risk to the Cook Islands is currently assessed as low. This proactive measure aims to safeguard the local poultry industry and prevent potential outbreaks.

analysis.brief_en: Brazil's Rio Grande do Sul state has confirmed its first case of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) in a backyard poultry flock in the municipality of Coqueiros do Sul. The diagnosis was officially confirmed by the Federal Agricultural Defense Laboratory in Campinas on July 17, 2026, following initial notification on July 14. This marks the state's first registered case of HPAI, prompting veterinary authorities to investigate and respond to the outbreak. The affected flock is located in the northwest region of Rio Grande do Sul, and authorities are monitoring the situation to prevent further spread of the virus.

news.content_title: EU says Turkey's bird flu is lethal H5N1 strain
news.content: EU says Turkey's bird flu is lethal H5N1 strain The number of deaths and sick people is on the rise across Turkey. Turkey January 7, 2006 Brussels (AsiaNews/ Agencies)  The bird flu virus which has reached Turkey is the lethal H5N1 strain: this was confirmed by the European Commission after laboratory testing in Weybridge. In a statement released today, it was noted that an EU ban on imports from Turkey of live birds and poultry products would remain. Meanwhile the number of deaths and sick people in the country is growing. A third child, Hulya Kocyigit, 11 years, from the family which already lost two children to bird flu, died yesterday. Her brother Mehemet Ali, 14 years died last week and her sister Fatima, aged 15 years, died on 14 January. The family lives near Van, nearly on the eastern border with Iran. A family of Sanliurfa, on the southern border with Syria was admitted to hospital and placed in isolation after they presented symptoms of bird flu. Ibrahim Sakat, his wife and two children felt ill after eating an infected chicken. Sakat is a poultry merchant. Doctors have at least 20 people under observation across all the territory of Turkey, most of them youth suspected to have contracted the lethal virus

news.content: Sign in Join Help VetSurgeon.org Home News Discussions Jobs Films Films All films Veterinary Controversies Veterinary Costs Talking Points Product Briefings Cardiology Dentistry Dermatology Diagnostic Imaging Equine Exotics Farm Animal Neurology Ophthalmology Orthopaedics Pathology/Cytology Soft Tissue Surgery Menu NEWS NEWS Email updates Email updates LATEST JOBS Derbyshire Small Animal Vet Bromley Small Animal Vet City of Rockingham Lead Surgical Veterinarian Stowmarket Small Animal Vet View all veterinary jobs Options Subscribe by email All Headlines >> Cambridgeshire vet recognised for leadership in avian influenza response and data-driven welfare Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Email Chris Ritchie VetSurgeon News /cfs-filesystemfile/__key/communityserver-components-sitefiles/graphics-logos/vetsurgeon_2D00_news.gif?_=636335966444922000 Comments 0 20 Jul 2026 7:00 AM Jessica Seale of Slate Hall Veterinary Services in Rampton, Cambridgeshire, was named the Zoetis-sponsored ‘Farm Vet of the Year’ at the recent National Egg & Poultry Awards ceremony in London. Jessica graduated at Bristol in 2020 and also has a MSc in One Health (infectious diseases) from RVC/London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine. She began her career in a Yorkshire poultry practice before joining Slate Hall in 2022, where she is now a senior associate. She played a key role in responding to avian influenza outbreaks, carrying out more than 400 bird flu licensing visits and contributing to industry working groups including the UK’s first avian influenza vaccination trials. The judges stated: “A strong advocate for welfare-led production, Jessica Seale has championed the use of anti-inflammatory treatments in broilers. She has also embraced technology to improve decision-making, developing automated data analysis tools that transform thousands of data points into real-time health insights for veterinary teams and producers. “Through her blend of science, innovation and collaboration, Seale continues to have a lasting effect on flock health, welfare and the future of the UK poultry industry.” Jessica also trains veterinary students and professionals, organises farm manager events and supports antibiotic monitoring programmes. The photo shows Jessica (centre) with Emily Hughes of Zoetis and host TV magician Ben Hanlin (credit Colin Miller). news.content_zh: 杰西卡·西尔 (Jessica Seale) 是剑桥郡 Slate Hall 兽医服务中心的高级助理,因其在 禽流感 应对措施和创新的数据驱动福利计划方面的卓越领导力而被授予 Zoetis 赞助的“年度农场兽医”称号。Seale 获得了伦敦国家蛋类和家禽奖的认可,已进行了 400 多次禽流感许可访问,并为英国首次 禽流感 疫苗接种 试验做出了贡献。她的工作包括开发自动化数据分析工具,将数千个数据点转化为兽医团队和生产者的实时健康见解。她是福利主导型生产的坚定倡导者,倡导肉鸡抗炎 治疗,并积极培训兽医学生和专业人员,同时支持抗生素监测计划。通过将科学、创新和合作融为一体,Seale 继续对鸡群健康、福利和英国家禽业的未来产生持久影响。

news.content: 《Animal Diseases》:Identification of two novel B-cell epitopes targeting the hemagglutinin protein of H9N2 avian influenza virus 编辑推荐: HA中已报道的线性B细胞表位数量有限,尤其在HA1内缺乏保守位点,成为开发广谱反应性诊断方法和疫苗的主要障碍。为此,研究人员开展了本研究,旨在鉴定H9N2 AIV HA蛋白中保守的线性B细胞表位,作为诊断检测的潜在靶点。 研究人员通过真核系统表达重组HA蛋白,制备单克隆抗体,系统鉴定出两个新的线性B细胞表位,并验证其关键残基、结构定位和保守性。该研究发表在《Animal Diseases》上。主要结论是:定义了H9N2 HA上的两个非中和表位,扩展了抗原图谱,为亚型特异性诊断检测提供了有前景的分子靶点。 为开展研究,研究人员使用了以下几个关键技术方法:采用真核表达系统(HEK293细胞)表达并纯化H9N2 HA-hFc融合蛋白;通过杂交瘤技术制备单克隆抗体(mAbs)9C12和9F4;利用ELISA、Western blot、免疫荧光(IFA)鉴定抗体结合特性,并用血凝抑制(HI)试验和中和试验评估中和活性;通过构建一系列N端EGFP标签的HA截短片段,在HEK293T细胞中表达后经Western blot进行表位作图,鉴定最小线性表位;采用丙氨酸扫描诱变确定关键残基;利用SWISS-MODEL同源建模和PyMOL可视化进行结构分析;使用基于NCBI数据库的30株代表性H9N2分离株及其他甲型流感病毒亚型的HA序列进行多重序列比对(CLUSTAL W、ESPript 3.0、WebLogo 3.0)分析保守性。病毒株来源为A/chicken/Hubei/222/2022(GenBank登录号PV342487)。 **Expression and generation of monoclonal antibodies targeting recombinant HA protein**:研究人员在HEK293细胞中表达重组H9N2 HA-hFc融合蛋白,经蛋白A亲和层析纯化,SDS?PAGE显示约90 kDa的单一条带(符合糖基化),Western blot用H9N2抗血清和抗人IgG确认成功表达。免疫BALB/c小鼠后获得两株杂交瘤9C12和9F4,ELISA筛选阳性,Western blot和IFA证实两者特异性识别H9N2感染MDCK细胞中的病毒HA。但HI试验和中和试验均显示无中和活性(IC 50 > 50 μg/mL),表明这两种mAbs识别非中和但抗原可及的HA区域。 **Fine mapping of the minimal linear B-cell epitope recognized by the monoclonal antibodies 9C12 and 9F4**:利用EGFP标签的HA截短片段在HEK293T细胞中表达,通过Western blot逐步缩小反应区域。对9C12,从HA1 (aa 19–338)开始,逐步定位至aa 96–195、aa 96–145、aa 116–135、aa 120–131,最终确定最小线性表位为 123FSSSRSYQ 130。对9F4,类似策略定位至HA1,再经aa 176–279、aa 176–225、aa 196–215,最终确定最小线性表位为 201NLYTRTDTT 209。表明9C12和9F4识别HA1内两个不同的连续抗原决定簇。 **Identification of critical residues within the minimal epitopes recognized by mAbs 9C12 and 9F4**:通过丙氨酸扫描诱变,将每个残基逐一替换为丙氨酸,Western blot检测抗体结合。对于9C12表位( 123FSSSRSYQ 130),S124、S125、R127、S128、Y129、Q130的替换消除结合,而F123和S126无影响,确定这六个残基为关键核心。对于9F4表位( 201NLYTRTDTT 209),N201、Y203、T204、T206、D207为必需,而L202、R205、T208、T209为非必需,定义了精确的氨基酸决定簇。 **Structural and antigenic analysis of the identified epitopes on the H9N2 HA protein**:利用DNAStar的PROTEAN模块进行免疫学特性预测,两个表位均显示强亲水性、高抗原指数和表面概率。通过SWISS-MODEL同源建模生成的H9N2 HA三聚体三维模型显示,两个表位均暴露于HA表面且溶剂可及。结构域定位表明, 201NLYTRTDTT 209位于受体结合亚结构域(紫色), 123FSSSRSYQ 130位于退化酯酶亚结构域(蓝色),表明9F4和9C12识别HA的不同功能区域,但均非中和表位。 **Conservation analysis of the 9C12 and 9F4 epitopes among AIV strains**:对30株代表性H9N2分离株的HA进行多重序列比对,9C12表位( 123FSSSRSYQ 130)总体保守,关键残基F123、S124、S125、S128、Y129、Q130高度稳定,S126和R127有轻微替换。9F4表位( 201NLYTRTDTT 209)在所有分析毒株中几乎完全不变,显示极强保守性。与其他甲型流感病毒亚型(H1–H13、H16)的比较表明,两个表位在非H9病毒中保守性低,提示它们具有亚型特异性保守特征,可作为H9N2检测的潜在分子标记。 209,与以往报道的集中于受体结合亚结构域(RBD)和退化酯酶亚结构域(VED)的中和表位不同,属于此前未表征的非中和表位。9C12表位位于VED,不与已知中和敏感残基重叠;9F4表位位于RBD,结合强表面暴露和H9N2毒株间近乎完全的保守性,使其区别于此前报道的抗原位点。关键残基分析(如S124、S125、R127等)以单残基分辨率提供了诊断设计的分子基础。传统HI试验存在交叉反应性,而靶向短线性表位的单克隆抗体(如9F4)可提高H9N2血清学检测的特异性,对野外监测和流行病学监测至关重要。尽管这些表位不能直接用于疫苗设计,但为肽基ELISA和侧流层析检测提供了验证靶点。 **结论**部分翻译为:总之,在H9N2 HA蛋白上鉴定出两个新的线性B细胞表位,并将其定性为具有诊断潜力的亚型相关抗原区域。尽管相应的单克隆抗体缺乏中和活性,但所鉴定的表位可能为H9N2特异性检测和未来监测应用提供有用的分子标记。

analysis.time: Published on 2026-07-23. Event date not explicitly reported in the evidence.
analysis.location_and_population: Research conducted using H9N2 avian influenza virus strains, with a focus on global poultry health implications. The study utilized a virus isolate from A/chicken/Hubei/222/2022 (GenBank PV342487).
analysis.event: Researchers identified two novel linear B-cell epitopes (123FSSSRSYQ130 and 201NLYTRTDTT209) on the hemagglutinin (HA) protein of H9N2 avian influenza virus. The study, published in Animal Diseases, confirmed these epitopes are non-neutralizing but highly conserved and surface-exposed, offering potential targets for subtype-specific diagnostic tests.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study involved 30 representative H9N2 strains and compared them with other influenza subtypes (H1-H13, H16). The 9F4 epitope (201NLYTRTDTT209) showed near-complete conservation across H9N2 strains, while both epitopes had low conservation in non-H9 subtypes. No cases, deaths, or direct public health impact were reported; the focus was on diagnostic and research applications.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The research employed advanced techniques including eukaryotic expression, monoclonal antibody generation, epitope mapping, and structural modeling. The study concluded that these epitopes could improve H9N2-specific serological detection but noted they are not suitable for vaccine design due to their non-neutralizing nature. The evidence is from a full original report with no unresolved limitations.

analysis.brief_en: A study published in Animal Diseases has identified two novel linear B-cell epitopes on the hemagglutinin protein of H9N2 avian influenza virus, offering promising targets for subtype-specific diagnostic tests. Researchers expressed the HA protein in a eukaryotic system and generated monoclonal antibodies 9C12 and 9F4, which recognized non-neutralizing but highly conserved epitopes: 123FSSSRSYQ130 in the esterase domain and 201NLYTRTDTT209 in the receptor-binding domain. Structural analysis confirmed both epitopes are surface-exposed, and conservation analysis showed the 9F4 epitope is nearly invariant across H9N2 strains. These findings expand the antigenic map of H9N2 HA and could enhance the specificity of serological surveillance for this virus, which poses ongoing threats to poultry health and has zoonotic potential.

faith in capitalism New Zealand begins vaccinating endangered birds after H5N1 detections Wednesday, 22 July 2026, 07:14 Dr Kate McInnes vaccinates a takahe at Willowbank, Christchurch, New Zealand, on behalf of the Department of Conservation. Officials raced to protect five critically endangered species after two H5N1 infections were detected, deploying emergency vaccinations and stricter biosecurity on bird colonies. As reported by CNN New Zealand is known on the world stage as a country with a special fascination for birds: mornings here ring with birdsong, and locals often refer to themselves as kiwis. Each year one of the country’s species receives the Bird of the Year title by popular vote. Last week, two birds infected with the deadly H5N1 avian influenza strain were recorded. Worldwide bird die-offs are causing millions of deaths, and nature lovers are worried: the preservation of the country’s unique natural treasures is at risk. New Zealand is one of the last large landmasses with isolated islands where for millions of years there were no mammalian megafaunal predators. It was a true paradise for birds – from the kākāpō, a nocturnal flightless parrot, to the takahē, a colorful ground-dwelling bird, almost dinosaur-like in appearance. In a bold move, the country is now vaccinating 300 pairs of birds from five critically endangered species to protect them from the virus. These birds are found only in New Zealand; they do not exist anywhere else in the world, so this matters to us. – Andrew Hoggard Threats and On-Site Measures The H5N1 strain has left its mark in many countries, having appeared in Europe, where it first emerged in 2020, and spreading to other regions; it has also affected animals – foxes, polar bears, tigers, sea lions, and even people in rare cases. So far it is unknown how New Zealand’s birds will encounter a potential mass outbreak. Some species may not notice this at all, while others will die in large numbers. Some species may not notice this at all, and others will die in large numbers. – Mary van Andel To head off developments, New Zealand has been regularly testing thousands of birds over the past year. Although only two infected birds have been detected so far, both are alive. In response, some producers are keeping free-flying birds indoors, the country’s oldest zoo canceled close contact with penguins, and the public is advised not to touch dead birds. Long ago, the Oceania region was the only region in the world without this strain, until last month when an infected seabird was spotted on a beach in Western Australia. On both Antipodes, the pathogen appeared in the same type of subantarctic seabird – the brown skua, an aggressive bird that often acts similarly to a crow. The lack of predatory mammals over a long period led to a different evolutionary path: such species as kiwi, kākāpō, takahē, and weka could move freely through forest undergrowth, hardly using flight. With the arrival of humans and the emergence of predators about 700 years ago, more than one-fifth of endemic species disappeared. In particular Haast’s Eagle – once the largest eagle in the world – disappeared along with its prey, including the South Island Giant Moa, a large flightless bird that stood up to 3.6 meters tall. Today, more than half of the 93 endemic species are considered “in serious danger,” according to a 2017 government report. Some species seem from a “second era” – such as takahē, kiwi, and kākāpō – they remain the only flightless representatives. The kākāpō became famous after one of them tried to interact with the head of the zoological institute in a documentary film; its movements on camera frightened viewers and became memes and a source of emojis. Birds, especially the kākāpō, may be at risk of avian influenza because most of the population – only about 235 individuals – are concentrated on a small island refuge off the coast of Raikura/Stewart Island. Ash Murray, the biosecurity manager at the Department of Conservation, noted: “There are many seabirds with which the kākāpō may interact... and this increases the risk for this species.” The virus is transmitted mainly through the droppings and saliva of infected birds, so seabirds and others that gather in large flocks are at risk. The risk also rises for predators who feed on carcasses. Kiwi are not yet on the list of vaccinated species: their population is around 70,000 – many live in the wild and do not gather in large flocks. Two of the rarest subspecies – rowi and Haast tokoeka – are likely to become the next vaccination step. In the Ōamaru colony, where visitors gather at sunset to see hundreds of little blue penguins, footwear disinfection requirements have been introduced to prevent the spread of the virus. “We introduced these measures to protect the birds,” explained Philippa Agnew, scientific and ecological manager at Ōamaru Penguins. In this colony there are about 700 penguins, another 500 live in the neighboring district; such density increases the risk of disease spread. Little penguins occur only in New Zealand and Australia... So the extent of impact remains unknown. – Philippa Agnew Nevertheless, scientists and authorities continue to monitor the situation and work on additional protection measures for the most vulnerable species. In sum, the country takes the threat seriously but is ready to act with understanding and planning. Gradual vaccination, monitoring, and restrictions at places where birds gather should form the backbone of New Zealand’s resilience of its natural heritage in the future. She is here to stay... This will be about how to help our species adapt better to the new threat – Andrew Hoggard Overall, the country is actively working to protect its unique birds and remains hopeful that, in light of the global disease, it will be able to preserve kiwi, kākāpō, takahē, and other forest and coastal dwellers from extinction. Don’t miss other news: Australian authorities have increased surveillance and testing after H5N1 was detected in migrating seabirds near South Australia, with samples taken and public warned to report dead or sick birds. Ukraine reports about 1,433,230 Russian military casualties as of 22 July Wednesday, 22 July 2026, 07:06 Russia has lost about 1,433,230 of its military personnel since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine (archival photo). New official figures from Ukraine’s General Staff reveal startling cumulative Russian losses and heavy equipment attrition, raising fresh questions about battlefield dynamics and data reliability. This is reported by General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine on Telegram. According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine as of the morning of July 22, Russia, during its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, has suffered significant losses among servicemen – about 1,433,230 people. In particular, losses over the last 24 hours amounted to about 1,330 people. The Ukrainian command also released data on destroyed or lost Russian equipment as of the same period. Below are the main figures according to the calculations of the Ministry of Defense and the General Staff: tanks – 12,163 (+2) armored fighting vehicles – 24,982 (+4) artillery systems – 46,492 (+57) rocket artillery systems – 1,958 (+3) air defense systems – 1,513 aircraft – 438 helicopters – 354 ground robotic systems – 1,981 (+11) operational-tactical unmanned aerial vehicles – 421,900 (+1,610) cruise missiles – 4,933 ships/boats – 34 submarines – 2 motor vehicles and tanker trucks – 123,702 (+355) special equipment – 4,450 (+9) Loss dynamics and expert assessments According to a CSIS (Center for Strategic and International Studies) study published on July 1, combined losses on both sides since the start of the war have surpassed two million killed and wounded service members. Russia officially does not disclose its losses. Moscow last reported the number of fatalities in September 2022 – 5,937. In May 2025, Russian outlets Meduza and Mediazona, based on named lists, estimated the Russian army’s total losses by the end of 2025 at about 352,000 people: of these, about 261,000 were killed and 90,000 were missing in action or dead due to court rulings, or deaths recorded with a delay of more than 180 days for other reasons. According to British intelligence data as of May 2026, since the start of the invasion in 2022, nearly 500,000 Russian soldiers have died. Kyiv had long withheld official casualty data, stating that they would be disclosed after the war; now information is published roughly once a year by the President of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelensky. on behalf of the Department of Conservation. Officials raced to protect five critically endangered species after two H5N1 infections were detected, deploying emergency vaccinations and stricter biosecurity on bird colonies. As reported by CNN New Zealand is known on the world stage as a country with a special fascination for birds: mornings here ring with birdsong, and locals often refer to themselves as kiwis. Each year one of the country’s species receives the Bird of the Year title by popular vote. Last week, two birds infected with the deadly H5N1 avian influenza strain were recorded. Worldwide bird die-offs are causing millions of deaths, and nature lovers are worried: the preservation of the country’s unique natural treasures is at risk. New Zealand is one of the last large landmasses with isolated islands where for millions of years there were no mammalian megafaunal predators. It was a true paradise for birds – from the kākāpō, a nocturnal flightless parrot, to the takahē, a colorful ground-dwelling bird, almost dinosaur-like in appearance. In a bold move, the country is now vaccinating 300 pairs of birds from five critically endangered species to protect them from the virus. These birds are found only in New Zealand; they do not exist anywhere else in the world, so this matters to us. – Andrew Hoggard Threats and On-Site Measures The H5N1 strain has left its mark in many countries, having appeared in Europe, where it first emerged in 2020, and spreading to other regions; it has also affected animals – foxes, polar bears, tigers, sea lions, and even people in rare cases. So far it is unknown how New Zealand’s birds will encounter a potential mass outbreak. Some species may not notice this at all, while others will die in large numbers. Some species may not notice this at all, and others will die in large numbers. – Mary van Andel To head off developments, New Zealand has been regularly testing thousands of birds over the past year. Although only two infected birds have been detected so far, both are alive. In response, some producers are keeping free-flying birds indoors, the country’s oldest zoo canceled close contact with penguins, and the public is advised not to touch dead birds. Long ago, the Oceania region was the only region in the world without this strain, until last month when an infected seabird was spotted on a beach in Western Australia. On both Antipodes, the pathogen appeared in the same type of subantarctic seabird – the brown skua, an aggressive bird that often acts similarly to a crow. The lack of predatory mammals over a long period led to a different evolutionary path: such species as kiwi, kākāpō, takahē, and weka could move freely through forest undergrowth, hardly using flight. With the arrival of humans and the emergence of predators about 700 years ago, more than one-fifth of endemic species disappeared. In particular Haast’s Eagle – once the largest eagle in the world – disappeared along with its prey, including the South Island Giant Moa, a large flightless bird that stood up to 3.6 meters tall. Today, more than half of the 93 endemic species are considered “in serious danger,” according to a 2017 government report. Some species seem from a “second era” – such as takahē, kiwi, and kākāpō – they remain the only flightless representatives. The kākāpō became famous after one of them tried to interact with the head of the zoological institute in a documentary film; its movements on camera frightened viewers and became memes and a source of emojis. Birds, especially the kākāpō, may be at risk of avian influenza because most of the population – only about 235 individuals – are concentrated on a small island refuge off the coast of Raikura/Stewart Island. Ash Murray, the biosecurity manager at the Department of Conservation, noted: “There are many seabirds with which the kākāpō may interact... and this increases the risk for this species.” The virus is transmitted mainly through the droppings and saliva of infected birds, so seabirds and others that gather in large flocks are at risk. The risk also rises for predators who feed on carcasses. Kiwi are not yet on the list of vaccinated species: their population is around 70,000 – many live in the wild and do not gather in large flocks. Two of the rarest subspecies – rowi and Haast tokoeka – are likely to become the next vaccination step. In the Ōamaru colony, where visitors gather at sunset to see hundreds of little blue penguins, footwear disinfection requirements have been introduced to prevent the spread of the virus. “We introduced these measures to protect the birds,” explained Philippa Agnew, scientific and ecological manager at Ōamaru Penguins. In this colony there are about 700 penguins, another 500 live in the neighboring district; such density increases the risk of disease spread. Little penguins occur only in New Zealand and Australia... So the extent of impact remains unknown. – Philippa Agnew Nevertheless, scientists and authorities continue to monitor the situation and work on additional protection measures for the most vulnerable species. In sum, the country takes the threat seriously but is ready to act with understanding and planning. Gradual vaccination, monitoring, and restrictions at places where birds gather should form the backbone of New Zealand’s resilience of its natural heritage in the future. She is here to stay... This will be about how to help our species adapt better to the new threat – Andrew Hoggard Overall, the country is actively working to protect its unique birds and remains hopeful that, in light of the global disease, it will be able to preserve kiwi, kākāpō, takahē, and other forest and coastal dwellers from extinction. analysis.brief_en: New Zealand has begun vaccinating endangered birds following the detection of H5N1 avian influenza in two birds. The Department of Conservation is vaccinating 300 pairs from five critically endangered species, including the takahe, to protect these unique birds found nowhere else in the world. The H5N1 strain has previously caused millions of bird deaths globally and has spread to various regions, including Australia.

Health)防范提供了关键早期预警,然而,整合宿主生态学、空间格局、季节性、病毒谱系和风险因素的国家尺度分析仍然有限。研究人员分析了2022年至2026年间加拿大野生动物高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)监测记录,以描述时空动态并识别与检测计数相关的因素。研究人员对13个省和地区的2657次检测进行了回顾性分析,使用描述性流行病学、空间聚类方法和负二项混合模型(Negative Binomial mixed models)。检测结果主要为禽类(93.3%),水禽和猛禽是主要宿主群体,而哺乳动物占较小但流行病学重要的比例(6.7%)。检测负担在2022年最高,秋季和春季活动增加。安大略省、阿尔伯塔省和不列颠哥伦比亚省被确定为主要热点地区,草原地区部分区域存在局部聚集。重配的欧亚-北美谱系(Eurasian–North American lineages)占主导地位(80.8%),并且与更高的检测计数密切相关。模型结果确定了年份、季节和谱系是关键预测因子。这些发现支持基于风险的“同一健康”监测,优先考虑高负担地区、迁徙相关时期、关键禽类宿主群体、重配病毒谱系,并持续监测哺乳动物野生动物。 研究背景与问题:高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)(HPAI A(H5N1))已成为一项日益严峻的“同一健康”(One Health)挑战,其传播动态涉及野生鸟类、家禽、哺乳动物野生动物、人类及共享环境。野生鸟类,尤其是水鸟,是禽流感病毒的主要储存宿主,而近期HPAI H5亚型2.3.4.4b分支(clade 2.3.4.4b)的泛动物疫情(panzootic)显著改变了该病毒的地理范围和宿主广度,导致野生鸟类大量死亡、家禽暴发及向哺乳动物的溢出增加。在加拿大,该病毒于2021年12月通过跨大西洋传入,随后基因组分析证实了多次野生鸟类引入及与北美禽流感病毒的广泛重配。尽管已有研究关注局部或特定类群的疫情,但缺乏整合多年、多省份、宿主类别、季节、迁徙期及病毒谱系的全国性尺度分析,以系统描述时空动态并识别风险因素。因此,本研究旨在填补这一空白,为基于风险的“同一健康”监测和预防性防范提供依据。 研究内容与结论:研究人员分析了2022年至2026年初加拿大野生动物HPAI A(H5N1)监测记录(共2657次检测),通过描述性流行病学、空间聚类(Global Moran's I和局部空间关联指标LISA)及负二项广义线性混合模型(Negative Binomial GLMM)识别风险因素。主要发现:检测负担在2022年最高,春、秋季显著高于冬季;安大略省、阿尔伯塔省和不列颠哥伦比亚省是主要热点地区,萨斯喀彻温省存在显著高-高聚类;水禽(44.0%)和猛禽(23.2%)是主要宿主群体,哺乳动物占6.7%;重配的欧亚-北美谱系(Reassortant Eurasian–North American lineages)占80.8%,与检测计数强相关;模型确认年份、季节和谱系是主要预测因子。基于这些发现,研究人员构建了靶向监测框架,回顾性评估显示可覆盖75.0%的历史检测。该研究发表在《Comparative Immunology, Microbiology and Infectious Diseases》。 关键技术方法:本研究为回顾性观察性研究,数据来源于加拿大食品检验局(CFIA)/ArcGIS平台及加拿大野生动物健康合作组织(CWHC)的公共高致病性禽流感野生动物仪表板,包含2022年至2026年实验室确诊的HPAI A(H5N1)检测记录,覆盖13个省和地区、112种野生动物物种。主要方法包括:描述性流行病学分析(时间、季节、宿主分布);空间自相关分析(Global Moran's I和LISA(局部空间关联指标));负二项广义线性混合模型(Negative Binomial generalised linear mixed model)用于风险因素建模,以检测计数(按省份、时间、宿主、谱系分层)为结局,纳入年份、季节、宿主类别、谱系等固定效应及省份和物种随机截距;并基于主要流行病学发现开发并回顾性评估了靶向监测框架。 研究结果: 3.1 数据集概述:最终数据集包含2657次检测,其中禽类占93.3%(2478次),哺乳动物占6.7%(179次),死亡相关记录占74.5%(1980次)。 3.2 检测的时间与季节分布:年度检测量差异显著,2022年最高(1199次,占45.1%),2023年(423次)、2024年(363次)下降,2025年回升至605次。季节上,秋季(34.1%)和春季(33.1%)检测量最高,冬季(21.9%)次之,夏季(10.9%)最低。迁徙期分析显示,秋季和春季迁徙期分别占34.1%和33.1%,非迁徙期亦占32.8%,表明疫情不限于迁徙事件。 3.3 2022年疫情波特征:2022年疫情波集中于魁北克省(17.4%)、不列颠哥伦比亚省(14.8%)、安大略省(14.3%)、萨斯喀彻温省(12.4%)和阿尔伯塔省(12.0%),合计占70.9%。宿主类别中,水禽(36.3%)和猛禽(26.7%)为主。病毒谱系以重配欧亚-北美谱系(76.5%)为主,全欧亚谱系占22.4%。 3.4 空间热点与地理聚类:省份层面,安大略省(618次)、阿尔伯塔省(429次)和不列颠哥伦比亚省(391次)为极高检测热点;魁北克省、萨斯喀彻温省和新斯科舍省为高检测省份。全局Moran's I无显著空间自相关(p=0.3266),局部Moran's I识别出萨斯喀彻温省为显著高-高聚类(p=0.0120),曼尼托巴省为显著低-高空间异常值(p=0.0074)。 3.5 宿主类别的地理变异:水禽在多数省份检测量最高,尤其魁北克省、不列颠哥伦比亚省、安大略省、萨斯喀彻温省和阿尔伯塔省;猛禽为次要重要宿主。海鸟和海鸥/燕鸥在加拿大大西洋省份(如新斯科舍省、纽芬兰与拉布拉多省)贡献较高,而水禽和猛禽在加拿大中部和西部主导。 3.6 宿主生态与病毒谱系模式:宿主类别中,水禽(44.0%,1170次)和猛禽(23.2%,617次)占主导,随后是鸦科(10.8%)、海鸥/燕鸥(8.6%)、哺乳动物(6.7%)和海鸟(5.2%)。谱系方面,重配欧亚-北美谱系占80.8%(2148次),全欧亚谱系占18.6%(494次)。 3.7 病毒谱系的地理分布:重配欧亚-北美谱系在几乎所有省份占主导,全欧亚谱系在多个省份有检出但频率较低,谱系未知记录罕见。检测数最高的省份与主要疫情区域一致。 3.8 风险因素建模数据集:建模数据集包含149,760个省份-时间-宿主-谱系分层,其中99.29%为零计数,方差与均值比(7.47)表明过度分散,支持负二项模型。 3.9 与HPAI检测计数相关的风险因素:负二项季节模型(AIC最低)显示,与2022年相比,2023-2026年检测计数显著降低(发病率比IRR范围0.03-0.28)。与冬季相比,秋季(IRR=1.51)和春季(IRR=1.39)检测计数更高,夏季更低(IRR=0.61)。全欧亚谱系(IRR=40.39)和重配欧亚-北美谱系(IRR=129.80)与检测计数强相关。 3.10 基于风险的HPAI监测框架:靶向监测框架优先考虑五个高负担省份、两种主要宿主类别(水禽和猛禽)及春、秋季。回顾性评估显示,该框架可捕获75.0%(1992/2657)的历史检测,年度覆盖率在70.1%-82.5%之间。 讨论与结论:研究发现检测模式受时间动态、地理变异、宿主生态学和病毒谱系共同驱动。春季和秋季检测高峰与迁徙和季节性聚集一致,但非迁徙期大量检测表明需全年监测。水禽和猛禽作为主要宿主,反映了其作为储存宿主和捕食/腐食暴露的角色。重配谱系的强关联提示病毒重配事件推动了疫情扩散。模型证实年份、季节和谱系是主要预测因子,负二项框架适合处理过度分散的监测数据。局限性包括基于检测数据而非真实感染率,可能受报告偏差影响;未纳入环境协变量;监测框架需外部验证。结论:加拿大野生动物HPAI A(H5N1)检测在时间、空间、宿主和病毒谱系上呈现明确结构,集中高负担省份、以禽类宿主(尤其水禽和猛禽)为主、春秋季高、重配谱系主导。这些发现支持基于风险的“同一健康”监测,优先考虑高负担地区、迁徙相关时期、水鸟和食腐相关宿主群体、重配病毒谱系,并持续监测哺乳动物野生动物。未来监测应整合野生动物、家养动物、环境、基因组和公共卫生数据,以加强早期预警和防范能力。 news.content_original: 加拿大野生动物中高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)的时空动态与生态风险因素:一项“同一健康”监测分析 《Comparative Immunology, Microbiology and Infectious Diseases》:Spatiotemporal dynamics and ecological risk factors of high pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in Canadian wildlife: A One Health surveillance analysis 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年07月23日 来源:Comparative Immunology, Microbiology and Infectious Diseases 2.0 高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)已在地理和生态上扩展,影响野生鸟类、哺乳动物野生动物、家养动物和人类。野生动物监测为“同一健康”(One Health)防范提供了关键早期预警,然而,整合宿主生态学、空间格局、季节性、病毒谱系和风险因素的国家尺度分析仍然有限。研究人员分析了2022年至2026年间加拿大野生动物高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)监测记录,以描述时空动态并识别与检测计数相关的因素。研究人员对13个省和地区的2657次检测进行了回顾性分析,使用描述性流行病学、空间聚类方法和负二项混合模型(Negative Binomial mixed models)。检测结果主要为禽类(93.3%),水禽和猛禽是主要宿主群体,而哺乳动物占较小但流行病学重要的比例(6.7%)。检测负担在2022年最高,秋季和春季活动增加。安大略省、阿尔伯塔省和不列颠哥伦比亚省被确定为主要热点地区,草原地区部分区域存在局部聚集。重配的欧亚-北美谱系(Eurasian–North American lineages)占主导地位(80.8%),并且与更高的检测计数密切相关。模型结果确定了年份、季节和谱系是关键预测因子。这些发现支持基于风险的“同一健康”监测,优先考虑高负担地区、迁徙相关时期、关键禽类宿主群体、重配病毒谱系,并持续监测哺乳动物野生动物。 研究背景与问题:高致病性禽流感A(H5N1)(HPAI A(H5N1))已成为一项日益严峻的“同一健康”(One Health)挑战,其传播动态涉及野生鸟类、家禽、哺乳动物野生动物、人类及共享环境。野生鸟类,尤其是水鸟,是禽流感病毒的主要储存宿主,而近期HPAI H5亚型2.3.4.4b分支(clade 2.3.4.4b)的泛动物疫情(panzootic)显著改变了该病毒的地理范围和宿主广度,导致野生鸟类大量死亡、家禽暴发及向哺乳动物的溢出增加。在加拿大,该病毒于2021年12月通过跨大西洋传入,随后基因组分析证实了多次野生鸟类引入及与北美禽流感病毒的广泛重配。尽管已有研究关注局部或特定类群的疫情,但缺乏整合多年、多省份、宿主类别、季节、迁徙期及病毒谱系的全国性尺度分析,以系统描述时空动态并识别风险因素。因此,本研究旨在填补这一空白,为基于风险的“同一健康”监测和预防性防范提供依据。 研究内容与结论:研究人员分析了2022年至2026年初加拿大野生动物HPAI A(H5N1)监测记录(共2657次检测),通过描述性流行病学、空间聚类(Global Moran's I和局部空间关联指标LISA)及负二项广义线性混合模型(Negative Binomial GLMM)识别风险因素。主要发现:检测负担在2022年最高,春、秋季显著高于冬季;安大略省、阿尔伯塔省和不列颠哥伦比亚省是主要热点地区,萨斯喀彻温省存在显著高-高聚类;水禽(44.0%)和猛禽(23.2%)是主要宿主群体,哺乳动物占6.7%;重配的欧亚-北美谱系(Reassortant Eurasian–North American lineages)占80.8%,与检测计数强相关;模型确认年份、季节和谱系是主要预测因子。基于这些发现,研究人员构建了靶向监测框架,回顾性评估显示可覆盖75.0%的历史检测。该研究发表在《Comparative Immunology, Microbiology and Infectious Diseases》。 关键技术方法:本研究为回顾性观察性研究,数据来源于加拿大食品检验局(CFIA)/ArcGIS平台及加拿大野生动物健康合作组织(CWHC)的公共高致病性禽流感野生动物仪表板,包含2022年至2026年实验室确诊的HPAI A(H5N1)检测记录,覆盖13个省和地区、112种野生动物物种。主要方法包括:描述性流行病学分析(时间、季节、宿主分布);空间自相关分析(Global Moran's I和LISA(局部空间关联指标));负二项广义线性混合模型(Negative Binomial generalised linear mixed model)用于风险因素建模,以检测计数(按省份、时间、宿主、谱系分层)为结局,纳入年份、季节、宿主类别、谱系等固定效应及省份和物种随机截距;并基于主要流行病学发现开发并回顾性评估了靶向监测框架。 研究结果: 3.1 数据集概述:最终数据集包含2657次检测,其中禽类占93.3%(2478次),哺乳动物占6.7%(179次),死亡相关记录占74.5%(1980次)。 3.2 检测的时间与季节分布:年度检测量差异显著,2022年最高(1199次,占45.1%),2023年(423次)、2024年(363次)下降,2025年回升至605次。季节上,秋季(34.1%)和春季(33.1%)检测量最高,冬季(21.9%)次之,夏季(10.9%)最低。迁徙期分析显示,秋季和春季迁徙期分别占34.1%和33.1%,非迁徙期亦占32.8%,表明疫情不限于迁徙事件。 3.3 2022年疫情波特征:2022年疫情波集中于魁北克省(17.4%)、不列颠哥伦比亚省(14.8%)、安大略省(14.3%)、萨斯喀彻温省(12.4%)和阿尔伯塔省(12.0%),合计占70.9%。宿主类别中,水禽(36.3%)和猛禽(26.7%)为主。病毒谱系以重配欧亚-北美谱系(76.5%)为主,全欧亚谱系占22.4%。 3.4 空间热点与地理聚类:省份层面,安大略省(618次)、阿尔伯塔省(429次)和不列颠哥伦比亚省(391次)为极高检测热点;魁北克省、萨斯喀彻温省和新斯科舍省为高检测省份。全局Moran's I无显著空间自相关(p=0.3266),局部Moran's I识别出萨斯喀彻温省为显著高-高聚类(p=0.0120),曼尼托巴省为显著低-高空间异常值(p=0.0074)。 3.5 宿主类别的地理变异:水禽在多数省份检测量最高,尤其魁北克省、不列颠哥伦比亚省、安大略省、萨斯喀彻温省和阿尔伯塔省;猛禽为次要重要宿主。海鸟和海鸥/燕鸥在加拿大大西洋省份(如新斯科舍省、纽芬兰与拉布拉多省)贡献较高,而水禽和猛禽在加拿大中部和西部主导。 3.6 宿主生态与病毒谱系模式:宿主类别中,水禽(44.0%,1170次)和猛禽(23.2%,617次)占主导,随后是鸦科(10.8%)、海鸥/燕鸥(8.6%)、哺乳动物(6.7%)和海鸟(5.2%)。谱系方面,重配欧亚-北美谱系占80.8%(2148次),全欧亚谱系占18.6%(494次)。 3.7 病毒谱系的地理分布:重配欧亚-北美谱系在几乎所有省份占主导,全欧亚谱系在多个省份有检出但频率较低,谱系未知记录罕见。检测数最高的省份与主要疫情区域一致。 3.8 风险因素建模数据集:建模数据集包含149,760个省份-时间-宿主-谱系分层,其中99.29%为零计数,方差与均值比(7.47)表明过度分散,支持负二项模型。 3.9 与HPAI检测计数相关的风险因素:负二项季节模型(AIC最低)显示,与2022年相比,2023-2026年检测计数显著降低(发病率比IRR范围0.03-0.28)。与冬季相比,秋季(IRR=1.51)和春季(IRR=1.39)检测计数更高,夏季更低(IRR=0.61)。全欧亚谱系(IRR=40.39)和重配欧亚-北美谱系(IRR=129.80)与检测计数强相关。 3.10 基于风险的HPAI监测框架:靶向监测框架优先考虑五个高负担省份、两种主要宿主类别(水禽和猛禽)及春、秋季。回顾性评估显示,该框架可捕获75.0%(1992/2657)的历史检测,年度覆盖率在70.1%-82.5%之间。 讨论与结论:研究发现检测模式受时间动态、地理变异、宿主生态学和病毒谱系共同驱动。春季和秋季检测高峰与迁徙和季节性聚集一致,但非迁徙期大量检测表明需全年监测。水禽和猛禽作为主要宿主,反映了其作为储存宿主和捕食/腐食暴露的角色。重配谱系的强关联提示病毒重配事件推动了疫情扩散。模型证实年份、季节和谱系是主要预测因子,负二项框架适合处理过度分散的监测数据。局限性包括基于检测数据而非真实感染率,可能受报告偏差影响;未纳入环境协变量;监测框架需外部验证。结论:加拿大野生动物HPAI A(H5N1)检测在时间、空间、宿主和病毒谱系上呈现明确结构,集中高负担省份、以禽类宿主(尤其水禽和猛禽)为主、春秋季高、重配谱系主导。这些发现支持基于风险的“同一健康”监测,优先考虑高负担地区、迁徙相关时期、水鸟和食腐相关宿主群体、重配病毒谱系,并持续监测哺乳动物野生动物。未来监测应整合野生动物、家养动物、环境、基因组和公共卫生数据,以加强早期预警和防范能力。 基于风险的HPAI监测框架:靶向监测框架优先考虑五个高负担省份、两种主要宿主类别(水禽和猛禽)及春、秋季。回顾性评估显示,该框架可捕获75.0%(1992/2657)的历史检测,年度覆盖率在70.1%-82.5%之间。讨论与结论:研究发现检测模式受时间动态、地理变异、宿主生态学和病毒谱系共同驱动。春季和秋季检测高峰与迁徙和季节性聚集一致,但非迁徙期大量检测表明需全年监测。水禽和猛禽作为主要宿主,反映了其作为储存宿主和捕食/腐食暴露的角色。重配谱系的强关联提示病毒重配事件推动了疫情扩散。模型证实年份、季节和谱系是主要预测因子,负二项框架适合处理过度分散的监测数据。局限性包括基于检测数据而非真实感染率,可能受报告偏差影响;未纳入环境协变量;监测框架需外部验证。结论:加拿大野生动物HPAI A(H5N1)检测在时间、空间、宿主和病毒谱系上呈现明确结构,集中高负担省份、以禽类宿主(尤其水禽和猛禽)为主、春秋季高、重配谱系主导。这些发现支持基于风险的“同一健康”监测,优先考虑高负担地区、迁徙相关时期、水鸟和食腐相关宿主群体、重配病毒谱系,并持续监测哺乳动物野生动物。未来监测应整合野生动物、家养动物、环境、基因组和公共卫生数据,以加强早期预警和防范能力。

news.content: More victims and losses caused by bird flu More victims and losses caused by bird flu China - Vietnam - Hong Kong February 10, 2004 Hanoi (AsiaNews/Agencies)  A three year-old boy died yesterday at Hanoi's National Children's Hospital while a medical team from Hong Kong visited the pediatric healthcare center. According to a doctor from the hospital, it is still unknown if the boy died of avian influenza or not. But the boy was said to have had symptoms typical of the bird flu epidemic and lived near the province of Ha Tay, which had been hit badly by the virus. Yesterday the death of a 27 year-old man from the province of Binh Phuoc was confirmed to be due to the H5N1 bird flu virus. The toll of victims in Vietnam alone has reached 14. While in Thailand 5 people have died so far. The group of doctors from Hong Kong was sent by the World Health Organization (WHO) and the Vietnamese government to look into ways of treating the epidemic and infected people. The H5N1 virus has spread to 13 provinces in China. Chinese health authorities have forbidden the use of non-government approved vaccines, after WHO animal disease specialist, Jeff Gilbert, warned they could make the virus's spread worse and mask its presence in birds. Many farmers use contraband-produced vaccines, which are sold at a smaller price, yet are of poor quality. In order to produce specific H5N1 vaccines, Guangdong have set aside 5 million yuan (about 625,000 US dollars). The Chinese village of Doman Sangli (Guangdong) has been isolated as a precautionary measure after Sunday, Feb. 8, when over 1000 chickens died at a village farm. Test results are still pending. According to the WHO's representative in China, Henk Bekedam, it is likely there are cases of human infection in the country, even if for the time being there is no proof. The United States is also suffering from the bird flu, even if in a lighter way than in Vietnam and Thailand. The bird flu has caused poultry consumption to drop worldwide. Chen Xiwen, vice-director of Hong Hong's Central Financial Work Leading Group, said that consumption of poultry should be encouraged, but with taking proper precautions. Excessive measures cause people not to eat chicken and this leads to serious losses on the part of farmers. Yeoh Eng-kiong, director of Hong Kong's Department of Health, Welfare and Nutrition, proposed culling all chickens in one central location. Meanwhile, the availability of live chickens in Hong Kong's markets has diminished by one third (around 40,000 chickens a day), while prices have increased to as high as 48 Hong Kong dollars a kilo. (MR)

news.title_zh: 禽流感造成更多受害者和损失 - 亚洲新闻
news.source_body_en: The news report highlights the ongoing impact of bird flu, particularly the H5N1 subtype, in several Asian countries. A three-year-old boy died at Hanoi's National Children's Hospital in February 2004, with symptoms typical of bird flu, though the cause of death remains uncertain. In Binh Phuoc province, a 27-year-old man's death was confirmed to be due to H5N1. Vietnam has reported 14 victims, and Thailand has seen 5 deaths. The H5N1 virus has spread to 13 provinces in China, prompting health authorities to ban non-approved vaccines and isolate a village in Guangdong. Poultry consumption has dropped globally, and in Hong Kong, live chicken availability has decreased by one third, with prices rising. The WHO suggests possible human infections in China, but no definitive proof has been established. The report also mentions the economic impact on farmers and the need for balanced poultry consumption with proper precautions.

Renewals Text Bundle Top-Ups Free Trial BirdGuides Podcast Birdwatch Buy Issues Buy Birdwatch Digital Archive Subscribe Renewals About Bookshop Resources Publications BirdGuides Travel Supplement 2026 Guide to Optics Species Guide Sites Birding Sites Locations England Scotland Wales Republic of Ireland Northern Ireland Africa Antarctica Asia Australasia Central America and the Caribbean Europe North America South America Listing My Lists Species Lists BirdGuides Travel BirdGuides Travel Tours BirdGuides Travel Trip Reports Tour Leaders BirdGuides Podcast Articles Bird Flu Impact Could Leave Major Gannet Colonies Depleted Until 2041 23/07/2026 Share Bird-flu impact could leave major gannet colonies depleted until 2041 fac1358f-04e4-4bfb-bb8b-29f31ecf9f98 Two of the world's largest Northern Gannet colonies are not expected to recover fully from the devastating impacts of the 2022 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI; bird flu) outbreak until at least 2041, according to a new study. Research published in Biological Conservation found that bird flu caused a dramatic increase in adult mortality at both Bass Rock, East Lothian, and Grassholm, Pembrokeshire, with the loss of breeding adults expected to suppress population recovery for decades. The study revealed annual adult mortality rose from an average of 6% to 33% at Bass Rock and from 11% to 47% at Grassholm during the outbreak. As a result, colony size declined by 26% at Bass Rock and 38% at Grassholm by 2023. Northern Gannet colonies could take years to recovery from the impacts of avian influenza (Donald Hutchins). Long road to recovery Using population modelling, researchers estimate that, even under favourable conditions, neither colony is likely to return to the size it would have reached without the outbreak before 2041. They caution that recovery could take even longer if further pressures affect the populations. Lead author Jude Lane, Marine Conservation Scientist at the RSPB, said the findings demonstrated the long-term consequences of the outbreak. "The bird flu outbreak in 2022 dealt an unprecedented deadly blow to UK seabirds and these findings show that key gannet colonies on Bass Rock and Grassholm will be impacted for decades to come," she said. Other pressures Senior author Jana Jeglinski, of Aarhus University, added that the losses could not be viewed in isolation, with gannets also facing increasing pressure from fisheries bycatch, plastic pollution and climate change. The authors argue the results warrant a reassessment of the Northern Gannet's global conservation status, which is currently listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List. Reference Lane, J, et al. 2026. HPAI drives a fourfold increase in adult gannet mortality which requires two decades recovery time. Biological Conservation. analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-23. Event period: 2022 bird flu outbreak with projected recovery until at least 2041.
analysis.location_and_population: Location: Bass Rock, East Lothian, and Grassholm, Pembrokeshire (UK). Affected population: Northern Gannet colonies.
analysis.event: Confirmed event: Research published in Biological Conservation found that the 2022 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI; bird flu) outbreak caused increased adult mortality in Northern Gannet colonies, suppressing population recovery for decades.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Cases: Annual adult mortality rose from 6% to 33% at Bass Rock and from 11% to 47% at Grassholm. Impact: Colony size declined by 26% at Bass Rock and 38% at Grassholm by 2023. Risk: Recovery could take longer if additional pressures (fisheries bycatch, plastic pollution, climate change) affect populations.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Response: Population modeling estimates colonies may not recover to pre-outbreak size before 2041 under favorable conditions. Uncertainty: Recovery could be prolonged by other stressors. The study calls for reassessment of the Northern Gannet's global conservation status.

analysis.brief_en: A new study published in Biological Conservation reveals that the 2022 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) outbreak has severely impacted Northern Gannet colonies in the UK. At Bass Rock and Grassholm, annual adult mortality surged to 33% and 47% respectively, causing colony declines of 26% and 38% by 2023. Population modeling indicates these colonies may not recover to pre-outbreak sizes until at least 2041, even under favorable conditions. Researchers warn that additional pressures like fisheries bycatch, plastic pollution, and climate change could further delay recovery. The findings highlight the long-term consequences of the outbreak and suggest a reassessment of the Northern Gannet's global conservation status, currently listed as Least Concern.
analysis.summary_en: A new study published in Biological Conservation reveals that the 2022 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) outbreak has severely impacted Northern Gannet colonies in the UK. At Bass Rock and Grassholm, annual adult mortality surged to 33% and 47% respectively, causing colony declines of 26% and 38% by 2023. Population modeling indicates these colonies may not recover to pre-outbreak sizes until at least 2041, even under favorable conditions. Researchers warn that additional pressures like fisheries bycatch, plastic pollution, and climate change could further delay recovery. The findings highlight the long-term consequences of the outbreak and suggest a reassessment of the Northern Gannet's global conservation status, currently listed as Least Concern.

news.content_zh: 《生物保护》杂志上发表的一项新研究表明,2022 年 高致病性禽流感 (HPAI) 暴发 严重影响了英国北部塘鹅栖息地。在 Bass Rock 和 Grassholm,年成虫 死亡率 分别激增至 33% 和 47%,导致到 2023 年菌落下降 26% 和 38%。种群模型表明,即使在有利的条件下,这些菌落至少要到 2041 年才能恢复到 死亡率 之前的大小。研究人员警告说,渔业兼捕、塑料污染和气候变化等额外压力可能会进一步推迟复苏。研究结果强调了 暴发 的长期后果,并建议重新评估北部塘鹅的全球保护状况,目前被列为最不受关注的地区。

22 七月 2026, 07:14 凯特·麦克因尼斯博士在新西兰基督城的威洛班克代表新西兰保护部为塔卡黑鸟接种疫苗。 两只感染H5N1的野鸟被发现,生态学家担心疫情可能威胁本土特有物种。政府已启动疫苗接种与严格监测措施以阻止蔓延。 CNN据〜称 新西兰在国际舞台因对鸟类的独特热爱而闻名:晨曦被鸟鸣唤醒,当地人常自称为“奇异鸟”(kiwi)。每年,该国的某一物种通过民众投票获得“年度鸟类”称号。 上周,发现两只感染高致病性H5N1禽流感病毒的鸟类。全球鸟类灭绝的链条正推向百万级死亡,保护者担忧:新西兰独特的自然珍宝正处于威胁之下。 新西兰是全球为数不多的大型陆地区域之一,拥有孤立的岛屿,数百万年来没有大型掠食性哺乳动物。这曾是鸟类的天堂——从夜行动性的无翼鹦鹉卡卡波到色彩斑斓的地面鸟塔卡赫(takahē),体态近似恐龙。 在这一非常举措下,政府正着手为五种极危鸟类中的约300对进行疫苗接种,以保护它们免受病毒侵袭。 这些鸟只在新西兰出现,全球其他地方都找不到,对我们意义重大。 – 安德鲁·霍加德 现场威胁与应对举措 高致病性H5N1病毒已在多国造成影响,从最初于2020年在欧洲出现,扩散至其他区域;它还波及多种动物——狐狸、北极熊、老虎、海狮,甚至在罕见情况下波及人类。 目前尚不清楚新西兰鸟类将如何应对潜在的大规模暴发。某些物种可能根本察觉不到,而其他物种则可能大量死亡。 一些物种可能根本察觉不到这一点,而其他物种将大量死亡。 – 玛丽·范安德尔 为防范事态升级,新西兰在过去一年定期对数千只鸟进行检测。 尽管目前仅发现两只感染鸟,且两者仍存活。为此,一些饲养者将自由活动的鸟类圈养在室内,全国最古老的动物园取消了与企鹅的密切接触,民众被提醒不要触摸死鸟。 很久以来,大洋洲地区曾是全球唯一未出现该毒株的区域,直到上月在西澳海滩发现一只感染的海鸟。在两极区域,病原体出现在同一种亚南极海鸟——棕色斯库亚(brown skua),这是一种攻击性强、常被视作类似乌鸦的海鸟。 长期缺乏掠食性哺乳动物,导致另一种进化路径:如kiwi、卡卡波、塔卡赫和威卡等,能够在森林地表层自由移动,几乎不靠飞行。 约700年前人类的到来及掠食者的出现,使得超过五分之一的本土物种灭绝。特别是哈斯特巨鹰——曾经世界上最大的猛禽——随猎物一起消失,其中包括南岛巨鸟,这种巨型无翼鸟身高可达3.6米。目前,93种本土物种中超过一半被列为“严重濒危”,据2017年政府报告。 有些物种似乎来自“第二纪元”——如塔卡赫、卡卡波——它们仍是现存的非飞行代表。卡卡波之所以为人熟知,是因为其中一只在纪录片中试图与动物研究所所长互动,其在镜头中的动作曾吓坏观众,成为网络段子与表情包的素材。 其中,卡卡波可能面临禽流感风险,因为其种群大多集中在位于拉基乌拉岛/斯图尔特岛沿岸的一个小岛屿避难地,约只有235只。生物安全项目主管阿什·默里在自然保护部表示:“有大量海鸟与卡卡波互动的情形,这增加了该物种的风险。” 病毒主要通过感染鸟类的粪便和唾液传播,因此海鸟和其他集群聚集的动物面临威胁。掠食者食死尸的风险也在上升。 疫苗接种清单中尚未包括“奇异鸟”(kiwi):它们的数量约为7万,只存在于野外,且并不聚集成大群。最稀有的两个亚种——Rowi 与哈斯特托科埃卡鸟——可能成为接下来接种的对象。 在奥阿马鲁企鹅群,游客傍晚聚集观看数百只小蓝企鹅时,已实施鞋部消毒要求以防止病毒传播。“我们推出这些措施来保护鸟类,” Ōamaru Penguins 科学与环境经理菲莉帕·埃格纽解释道。 在奥阿马鲁企鹅群约有700只企鹅,邻近地区还有约500只;这种密度提高了疾病传播的风险。 小蓝企鹅仅分布在新西兰与澳大利亚......因此其影响程度尚不明确。 – 菲莉帕·埃格纽 尽管如此,科学家与当局继续监测形势,并努力制定对最脆弱物种的更多保护措施。 总之,新西兰对威胁保持认真对待,但也愿意以理解和周密的规划来行动。渐进式疫苗接种、监测与对鸟类聚集地的限制将成为未来保护新西兰自然遗产的基石。 它将留在这里......这是关于帮助我们的物种更好地适应新威胁的讨论 – 安德鲁·霍加德 总体而言,新西兰正积极保护其独特鸟类,并寄望在全球性疾病的背景下,能够保护好奇异鸟、卡卡波、塔卡赫及其他林海与海岸的居民,避免灭绝。 这里还有推荐内容: 惠灵顿机场晚间发生火灾,航站楼西南侧受损,多趟航班临时改降或取消,机场與消防正調查起火原因並逐步恢復運營。 H5N1在希德岛与麦克唐纳群岛爆发,约1.3万幼崽死亡,研究者警告亚南极生态面临严重威胁并呼吁加强监测与样本分析。 刚果(金)埃博拉确诊病例升至1502例,官方与专家警告真实数字可能更高,呼吁加强疫控、扩大国际协调与资金支持。

22 七月 2026, 07:14 凯特·麦克因尼斯博士在新西兰基督城的威洛班克代表新西兰保护部为塔卡黑鸟接种疫苗。 两只感染H5N1的野鸟被发现,生态学家担心疫情可能威胁本土特有物种。政府已启动疫苗接种与严格监测措施以阻止蔓延。 CNN据〜称 新西兰在国际舞台因对鸟类的独特热爱而闻名:晨曦被鸟鸣唤醒,当地人常自称为“奇异鸟”(kiwi)。每年,该国的某一物种通过民众投票获得“年度鸟类”称号。 目前尚不清楚新西兰鸟类将如何应对潜在的大规模暴发。某些物种可能根本察觉不到,而其他物种则可能大量死亡。 一些物种可能根本察觉不到这一点,而其他物种将大量死亡。 – 玛丽·范安德尔 为防范事态升级,新西兰在过去一年定期对数千只鸟进行检测。 尽管目前仅发现两只感染鸟,且两者仍存活。为此,一些饲养者将自由活动的鸟类圈养在室内,全国最古老的动物园取消了与企鹅的密切接触,民众被提醒不要触摸死鸟。 analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-21. Event date: Wednesday, 22 July 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: New Zealand, specifically Christchurch (Willowbank) and Ōamaru Penguin Colony. Affected population: Wild birds, including endangered species like takahē, kākāpō, and little blue penguins.
analysis.event: Confirmed discovery of two wild birds infected with highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza. The New Zealand Department of Conservation has initiated emergency vaccination for endangered species and implemented strict monitoring measures to prevent spread.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Two infected birds identified, both still alive. Risk to unique native species is high due to their evolutionary isolation and lack of immunity. Over 50% of New Zealand's 93 native bird species are classified as 'critically endangered'. The virus poses a threat through fecal and saliva transmission, particularly in densely populated bird habitats.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Vaccination underway for approximately 300 pairs of five critically endangered bird species. Regular testing of thousands of birds conducted over the past year. Additional measures include restricting free-ranging birds to indoor enclosures, canceling close contact with penguins at zoos, and public advisories against touching dead birds. Uncertainty remains about how different species will respond to potential outbreaks.

analysis.brief_en: New Zealand has confirmed two cases of H5N1 avian influenza in wild birds, prompting urgent action to protect the country's unique and endangered bird species. The Department of Conservation has launched an emergency vaccination program targeting five critically endangered species, including takahē and kākāpō. Despite only two infected birds being identified so far, both still alive, authorities are implementing strict monitoring and biosecurity measures due to the high vulnerability of New Zealand's native birds, which evolved in isolation without natural predators. The virus, which has spread globally since 2020, poses a significant threat to species with no prior exposure, potentially leading to mass mortalities. Conservation efforts include testing thousands of birds, restricting access to penguin colonies, and public warnings against handling dead birds.

news.source_body_en: New Zealand has confirmed two cases of H5N1 avian influenza in wild birds, prompting urgent action to protect the country's unique and endangered bird species. The Department of Conservation has launched an emergency vaccination program targeting five critically endangered species, including takahē and kākāpō. Despite only two infected birds being identified so far, both still alive, authorities are implementing strict monitoring and biosecurity measures due to the high vulnerability of New Zealand's native birds, which evolved in isolation without natural predators. The virus, which has spread globally since 2020, poses a significant threat to species with no prior exposure, potentially leading to mass mortalities. Conservation efforts include testing thousands of birds, restricting access to penguin colonies, and public warnings against handling dead birds.
news.content_zh: 新西兰在 野生鸟类 中确认了两例 H5N1 禽流感 病例,促使采取紧急行动保护该国独特的濒危鸟类。环境保护部启动了一项针对五种极度濒危物种的紧急 疫苗接种 计划,其中包括 takahē 和 kākāpō。尽管到目前为止只发现了两只受感染的鸟类,而且它们都还活着,但由于新西兰本土鸟类在没有天敌的情况下孤立进化,其高度脆弱性,当局正在实施严格的监测和生物安全措施。该病毒自 2020 年以来在全球传播,对之前没有接触过的物种构成了重大威胁,可能导致大规模死亡。保护工作包括测试数千只鸟类、限制进入企鹅栖息地以及公开警告不要处理死鸟。
news.summary_zh: 新西兰在 野生鸟类 中确认了两例 H5N1 禽流感 病例,促使采取紧急行动保护该国独特的濒危鸟类。环境保护部启动了一项针对五种极度濒危物种的紧急 疫苗接种 计划,其中包括 takahē 和 kākāpō。尽管到目前为止只发现了两只受感染的鸟类,而且它们都还活着,但由于新西兰本土鸟类在没有天敌的情况下孤立进化,其高度脆弱性,当局正在实施严格的监测和生物安全措施。该病毒自 2020 年以来在全球传播,对之前没有接触过的物种构成了重大威胁,可能导致大规模死亡。保护工作包括测试数千只鸟类、限制进入企鹅栖息地以及公开警告不要处理死鸟。

analysis_zh.location_and_population: 新西兰,特别是基督城(柳岸)和奥玛鲁企鹅栖息地。受影响种群:野生鸟类,包括塔卡赫、鸮鹦鹉和小蓝企鹅等濒临灭绝的物种。
analysis_zh.event: 确认发现两只野生鸟类感染高致病性H5N1 禽流感。新西兰环保部已针对濒危物种启动紧急疫苗接种,并实施严格的监测措施,防止扩散。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 发现了两只受感染的鸟,它们都还活着。由于独特的本地物种在进化上孤立且缺乏免疫力,因此它们面临的风险很高。新西兰 93 种本土鸟类中,超过 50% 被列为“极度濒危”。该病毒通过粪便和唾液 传播 构成威胁,特别是在人口稠密的鸟类栖息地。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 疫苗接种 正在进行中,旨在针对五种极度濒危鸟类中的约 300 对鸟类。过去一年对数千只鸟类进行了定期测试。其他措施包括将自由放养的鸟类限制在室内围栏内,取消与动物园企鹅的密切接触,以及禁止触摸死鸟的公共建议。不同物种将如何应对潜在的 暴发 仍存在不确定性。
